verses.1:1: In the beginning the Word existed, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
verses.1:2: This One was with God in the beginning.
verses.1:3: All things came into being through Him, and apart from Him not even one thing came into being. What has come into being
verses.1:4: in Him was life, and that life was the light of people.
verses.1:5: And the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not overtake it.
verses.1:6: There appeared a man sent from God; his name was John.
verses.1:7: This man came for testimony, so that he might testify concerning the light, so that everyone might believe through him.
verses.1:8: That man was not the light, but came so that he might testify concerning the light.
verses.1:9: The true light, which illuminates every person, was coming into the world.
verses.1:10: He was in the world, and the world came into being through Him, yet the world did not know Him.
verses.1:11: He came to His own domain, and His own people did not accept Him.
verses.1:12: Yet to as many as received Him, He gave them authority to become children of God, to those believing in His name,
verses.1:13: who were born not from bloodlines, nor from the desire of flesh, nor from the desire of a husband, but from God.
verses.1:14: And the Word became flesh and dwelt among us, and we gazed upon His glory, glory as of an only-begotten from a father, full of grace and truth.
verses.1:15: (John testifies concerning Him and has cried out, saying, "This was He of whom I said, 'The One coming after me has come ahead of me, because He existed before me.'")
verses.1:16: Because out of His fullness all of us received, even grace in place of grace;
verses.1:17: because the law was given through Moses; grace and truth came into being through Jesus Christ.
verses.1:18: No one has ever seen God; the only-begotten God, the One who is at the Father's side, He has made Him known.
verses.1:19: And this is the testimony of John, when the Jews sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him, "Who are you?"
verses.1:20: And he confessed and did not deny, and he confessed, "I am not the Christ."
verses.1:21: And they asked him, "What then? Are you Elijah?" And he says, "I am not." "Are you the Prophet?" And he answered, "No."
verses.1:22: Therefore they said to him, "Who are you, so that we may give an answer to those who sent us? What do you say concerning yourself?"
verses.1:23: He said, "I am a voice of one crying out in the wilderness, 'Make straight the way of the Lord,' just as Isaiah the prophet said."
verses.1:24: Now those who had been sent were from the Pharisees.
verses.1:25: And they asked him and said to him, "Why then are you baptizing, if you are not the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the Prophet?"
verses.1:26: John answered them, saying, "I baptize in water; among you stands One whom you do not know,
verses.1:27: the One coming after me, the strap of whose sandal I am not worthy to untie."
verses.1:28: These things happened in Bethany across the Jordan, where John was baptizing.
verses.1:29: On the next day he sees Jesus coming toward him and says, "Look, the Lamb of God who takes away the sin of the world!
verses.1:30: This is He on behalf of whom I said, 'After me comes a man who has come ahead of me, because He existed before me.'
verses.1:31: And I myself did not know Him, but so that He might be revealed to Israel, for this reason I came baptizing in water."
verses.1:32: And John testified, saying, "I have gazed upon the Spirit descending like a dove out of heaven, and He remained upon Him.
verses.1:33: And I myself did not know Him, but the One who sent me to baptize in water, that One said to me, 'Upon whomever you see the Spirit descending and remaining upon Him, this is the One who baptizes in the Holy Spirit.'
verses.1:34: And I myself have seen and have testified that this is the Son of God."
verses.1:35: On the next day again John was standing, along with two of his disciples,
verses.1:36: and looking closely at Jesus as He was walking, he says, "Look, the Lamb of God!"
verses.1:37: And the two disciples heard him speaking and followed Jesus.
verses.1:38: Now Jesus, turning and seeing them following, says to them, "What are you seeking?" And they said to Him, "Rabbi" (which translated means "Teacher"), "where are You staying?"
verses.1:39: He says to them, "Come and you will see." So they came and saw where He was staying, and they stayed with Him that day; it was about the tenth hour.
verses.1:40: Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, was one of the two who heard from John and followed Him.
verses.1:41: This man first finds his own brother Simon and says to him, "We have found the Messiah" (which translated is "Christ").
verses.1:42: He brought him to Jesus. Looking closely at him, Jesus said, "You are Simon, the son of John; you will be called Cephas" (which is translated "Peter").
verses.1:43: On the next day He wanted to go out into Galilee. And Jesus finds Philip and says to him, "Follow Me."
verses.1:44: Now Philip was from Bethsaida, from the city of Andrew and Peter.
verses.1:45: Philip finds Nathanael and says to him, "We have found the one of whom Moses wrote in the law, and also the prophets: Jesus, son of Joseph, the one from Nazareth."
verses.1:46: And Nathanael said to him, "Can anything good be from Nazareth?" Philip says to him, "Come and see."
verses.1:47: Jesus saw Nathanael coming toward Him and says concerning him, "Look, truly an Israelite in whom there is no deceit!"
verses.1:48: Nathanael says to Him, "Where do You know me from?" Jesus answered and said to him, "Before Philip called you, when you were under the fig tree, I saw you."
verses.1:49: Nathanael answered Him, "Rabbi, You are the Son of God; You are King of Israel!"
verses.1:50: Jesus answered and said to him, "Because I told you that I saw you under the fig tree, do you believe? You will see greater things than these."
verses.1:51: And He says to him, "Truly, truly, I tell you, you will see heaven opened and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man."
verses.2:1: And on the third day a wedding took place in Cana of Galilee, and the mother of Jesus was there.
verses.2:2: Now Jesus and His disciples were also invited to the wedding.
verses.2:3: And when the wine ran out, the mother of Jesus said to Him, "They have no wine."
verses.2:4: And Jesus said to her, "What is that to Me and to you, woman? My hour has not yet arrived."
verses.2:5: His mother said to the servants, "Whatever He tells you, do it."
verses.2:6: Now six stone water jars were set there according to the purification of the Jews, each holding two or three measures.
verses.2:7: Jesus said to them, "Fill the water jars with water." And they filled them to the top.
verses.2:8: And He said to them, "Draw some out now and bring it to the banquet steward." And they brought it.
verses.2:9: When the banquet steward tasted the water that had become wine, and did not know where it came from—though the servants who had drawn the water knew—the banquet steward called the bridegroom,
verses.2:10: and said to him, "Every person serves the good wine first, and when they have drunk freely, the lesser wine; you have kept the good wine until now."
verses.2:11: Jesus performed this as the beginning of the signs in Cana of Galilee and revealed His glory, and His disciples believed in Him.
verses.2:12: After this He went down to Capernaum, He and His mother and His brothers and His disciples; and they stayed there not many days.
verses.2:13: And the Passover of the Jews was near, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
verses.2:14: And He found in the temple those who were selling oxen and sheep and doves, and the moneychangers sitting there,
verses.2:15: and having made a whip of cords, He drove all of them out of the temple, both the sheep and the oxen, and He poured out the coins of the moneychangers and overturned the tables.
verses.2:16: And to those who were selling the doves He said, "Take these things away from here; stop making My Father's house a house of trade."
verses.2:17: His disciples remembered that it is written, "Zeal for Your house will consume Me."
verses.2:18: Therefore the Jews answered and said to Him, "What sign do You show us, seeing that You do these things?"
verses.2:19: Jesus answered and said to them, "Destroy this sanctuary, and in three days I will raise it up."
verses.2:20: Therefore the Jews said, "This sanctuary was built over forty-six years, and will You raise it up in three days?"
verses.2:21: But He was speaking about the sanctuary of His body.
verses.2:22: So when He was raised from the dead, His disciples remembered that He had been saying this; and they believed the Scripture and the word that Jesus had spoken.
verses.2:23: Now while He was in Jerusalem at the Passover, during the feast, many believed in His name, observing His signs that He was performing.
verses.2:24: Yet Jesus Himself was not entrusting Himself to them, because He knew all people,
verses.2:25: and because He had no need for anyone to testify about man, for He Himself knew what was in man.
verses.3:1: Now there was a man of the Pharisees named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews.
verses.3:2: This man came to Him by night and said to Him, "Rabbi, we know that You have come from God as a teacher; for no one is able to perform these signs that You perform unless God is with him."
verses.3:3: Jesus answered and said to him, "Truly, truly, I tell you, unless someone is born from above, he cannot see the kingdom of God."
verses.3:4: Nicodemus said to Him, "How can a man be born when he is old? He cannot enter into his mother's womb a second time and be born, can he?"
verses.3:5: Jesus answered, "Truly, truly, I tell you, unless someone is born of water and Spirit, he cannot enter into the kingdom of God.
verses.3:6: What has been born of the flesh is flesh, and what has been born of the Spirit is spirit.
verses.3:7: Do not be amazed that I said to you, 'You must be born from above.'
verses.3:8: The wind blows where it wishes, and you hear its sound, yet you do not know where it comes from and where it is going; so it is with everyone who has been born of the Spirit."
verses.3:9: Nicodemus answered and said to Him, "How can these things happen?"
verses.3:10: Jesus answered and said to him, "Are you the teacher of Israel, and you do not understand these things?
verses.3:11: Truly, truly, I tell you that we speak what we know and testify to what we have seen, yet you do not accept our testimony.
verses.3:12: If I told you earthly things and you do not believe, how will you believe if I tell you heavenly things?
verses.3:13: And no one has ascended into heaven except the One who descended from heaven, the Son of Man.
verses.3:14: And just as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so the Son of Man must be lifted up,
verses.3:15: so that everyone who believes in Him may have eternal life.
verses.3:16: For God loved the world in such a way that He gave His only-begotten Son, so that everyone who believes in Him may not perish, but have eternal life.
verses.3:17: For God did not send the Son into the world to judge the world, but so that the world might be saved through Him.
verses.3:18: The one who believes in Him is not judged; but the one who does not believe has already been judged, because he has not believed in the name of the only-begotten Son of God.
verses.3:19: Now this is the judgment: that the light has come into the world, and people loved the darkness rather than the light, for their deeds were evil.
verses.3:20: For everyone who practices wicked things hates the light and does not come to the light, so that his deeds may not be exposed.
verses.3:21: But the one who does the truth comes to the light, so that his deeds may be revealed as having been carried out in God."
verses.3:22: After these things Jesus and His disciples came into the land of Judea, and He was staying there with them and baptizing.
verses.3:23: Now John was also baptizing in Aenon near Salim, because there was much water there; and people were coming and being baptized.
verses.3:24: For John had not yet been thrown into prison.
verses.3:25: Therefore a dispute arose on the part of John's disciples with a Jew about purification.
verses.3:26: And they came to John and said to him, "Rabbi, the One who was with you across the Jordan, to whom you have testified—look, He is baptizing, and all are coming to Him."
verses.3:27: John answered and said, "A person cannot receive even one thing unless it has been given to him from heaven.
verses.3:28: You yourselves testify for me that I said, 'I am not the Christ,' but rather, 'I have been sent ahead of Him.'
verses.3:29: The one who has the bride is the bridegroom; yet the friend of the bridegroom, who stands and listens to him, rejoices with joy because of the bridegroom's voice. Therefore this joy of mine has been made full.
verses.3:30: He must increase, while I must decrease."
verses.3:31: The One who comes from above is above all. The one who is from the earth is of the earth and speaks from the earth; the One who comes from heaven is above all.
verses.3:32: What He has seen and heard, this He testifies to, and no one accepts His testimony.
verses.3:33: The one who has accepted His testimony has set his seal that God is true.
verses.3:34: For the One whom God sent speaks the words of God, for He does not give the Spirit by measure.
verses.3:35: The Father loves the Son and has given all things into His hand.
verses.3:36: The one who believes in the Son has eternal life; but the one who disobeys the Son will not see life, but the wrath of God remains on him.
verses.4:1: So when the Lord learned that the Pharisees had heard that Jesus was making and baptizing more disciples than John—
verses.4:2: though Jesus Himself was not baptizing, but His disciples were—
verses.4:3: He left Judea and went away again into Galilee.
verses.4:4: Now it was necessary for Him to pass through Samaria.
verses.4:5: So He came to a city of Samaria named Sychar, near the plot of land that Jacob gave to Joseph his son;
verses.4:6: and Jacob's spring was there. Therefore Jesus, exhausted from the journey, was sitting just as He was beside the spring; it was about the sixth hour.
verses.4:7: A woman from Samaria came to draw water. Jesus said to her, "Give Me a drink."
verses.4:8: For His disciples had gone away into the city in order to buy food.
verses.4:9: Then the Samaritan woman said to Him, "How is it that You, being a Jew, ask me for a drink, when I am a Samaritan woman?" For Jews do not have dealings with Samaritans.
verses.4:10: Jesus answered and said to her, "If you knew the gift of God and who the One is who is saying to you, 'Give Me a drink,' you yourself would have asked Him, and He would have given living water to you."
verses.4:11: The woman said to Him, "Sir, You have no bucket, and the well is deep; where then do You get this living water?
verses.4:12: You are not greater than our father Jacob, are You, who gave us the well and drank from it himself, along with his sons and his livestock?"
verses.4:13: Jesus answered and said to her, "Everyone who drinks from this water will thirst again;
verses.4:14: but whoever drinks from the water that I will give him will certainly never thirst; rather, the water that I will give him will become in him a spring of water leaping up into eternal life."
verses.4:15: The woman said to Him, "Sir, give me this water, so that I will not be thirsty nor keep coming all the way here to draw."
verses.4:16: He said to her, "Go, summon your husband, and come here."
verses.4:17: The woman answered and said to Him, "I do not have a husband." Jesus said to her, "You have rightly said, 'A husband I do not have';
verses.4:18: for you have had five husbands, and the one whom you now have is not your husband; this you have spoken truthfully."
verses.4:19: The woman said to Him, "Sir, I see that You are a prophet.
verses.4:20: Our fathers worshiped on this mountain, and you say that in Jerusalem is the place where one must worship."
verses.4:21: Jesus said to her, "Believe Me, woman, that an hour is coming when you will worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem.
verses.4:22: You worship what you do not know; we worship what we know, because salvation is from the Jews.
verses.4:23: Yet an hour is coming, and is here now, when the true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth; for indeed the Father seeks such people as those who worship Him.
verses.4:24: God is spirit, and it is necessary for those worshiping Him to worship in spirit and truth."
verses.4:25: The woman said to Him, "I know that Messiah is coming, the One who is called Christ; when that One comes, He will announce all things to us."
verses.4:26: Jesus said to her, "I am He, the One speaking to you."
verses.4:27: And at this point His disciples arrived, and they were marveling that He was speaking with a woman; yet no one said, "What are You seeking?" or, "Why are You speaking with her?"
verses.4:28: So the woman left her water jar behind, went away into the city, and said to the people,
verses.4:29: "Come, see a man who told me all the things that I did! Could this possibly be the Christ?"
verses.4:30: They came out from the city and were coming to Him.
verses.4:31: In the meantime, the disciples were urging Him, saying, "Rabbi, eat."
verses.4:32: But He said to them, "I have food to eat that you yourselves do not know."
verses.4:33: So the disciples were saying to one another, "No one brought Him anything to eat, did they?"
verses.4:34: Jesus said to them, "My food is to do the will of the One who sent Me and to bring His work to completion.
verses.4:35: Do you not say, 'There are still four months, and the harvest comes'? Look, I tell you, lift up your eyes and observe the fields, that they are white for harvest. Already
verses.4:36: the one who reaps is receiving wages and is gathering fruit for eternal life, so that the one who sows and the one who reaps may rejoice together.
verses.4:37: For in this the saying is true: 'One is the sower, and another is the reaper.'
verses.4:38: I Myself sent you to reap what you yourselves have not labored for; others have labored, and you have entered into their labor."
verses.4:39: Now from that city many of the Samaritans believed in Him because of the word of the woman who was testifying, "He told me all the things that I did."
verses.4:40: So when the Samaritans came to Him, they were asking Him to stay with them; and He stayed there two days.
verses.4:41: And far more believed because of His word,
verses.4:42: and they were saying to the woman, "No longer do we believe because of your speech; for we have heard for ourselves, and we know that this One is truly the Savior of the world."
verses.4:43: Now after the two days, He departed from there into Galilee;
verses.4:44: for Jesus Himself testified that a prophet has no honor in his own homeland.
verses.4:45: So when He arrived in Galilee, the Galileans welcomed Him, having seen all the things that He had done in Jerusalem at the feast; for they themselves also had gone to the feast.
verses.4:46: Therefore He came again to Cana of Galilee, where He had made the water wine. And there was a certain royal official whose son was sick in Capernaum.
verses.4:47: Having heard that Jesus had arrived from Judea into Galilee, this man went to Him and kept asking that He would come down and heal his son, for he was about to die.
verses.4:48: Therefore Jesus said to him, "Unless you see signs and wonders, you will by no means believe."
verses.4:49: The royal official said to Him, "Sir, come down before my little child dies."
verses.4:50: Jesus said to him, "Go on your way; your son is alive." The man believed the word that Jesus spoke to him and set off on his way.
verses.4:51: And while he was already going down, his slaves met him, saying that his boy was alive.
verses.4:52: Therefore he inquired from them the hour at which he had taken a turn for the better. So they told him, "Yesterday, at the seventh hour, the fever left him."
verses.4:53: So the father recognized that it was at that very hour in which Jesus had said to him, "Your son is alive"; and he himself believed, along with his entire household.
verses.4:54: Now this again was a second sign that Jesus performed after coming out of Judea into Galilee.
verses.5:1: After these things there was a feast of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
verses.5:2: Now there is in Jerusalem, by the Sheep Gate, a pool called Bethzatha in Hebrew, having five porticoes.
verses.5:3: In these lay a multitude of the sick—blind, lame, withered.
verses.5:5: Now a certain man was there who had been thirty-eight years in his illness.
verses.5:6: When Jesus saw him lying there and knew that he had already been that way for a long time, He said to him, "Do you want to become well?"
verses.5:7: The sick man answered Him, "Sir, I have no one to put me into the pool when the water is stirred up; and while I am coming, another goes down ahead of me."
verses.5:8: Jesus said to him, "Get up, pick up your mat, and walk."
verses.5:9: And immediately the man became well, and he picked up his mat and began walking. Now it was a Sabbath on that day.
verses.5:10: So the Jews were saying to the man who had been cured, "It is the Sabbath, and it is not lawful for you to carry the mat."
verses.5:11: But he answered them, "The One who made me well, He said to me, 'Pick up your mat and walk.'"
verses.5:12: They asked him, "Who is the man who said to you, 'Pick it up and walk'?"
verses.5:13: But the man who had been healed did not know who He was, for Jesus had slipped away, as there was a crowd in that place.
verses.5:14: After these things Jesus found him in the temple and said to him, "Look, you have become well; do not sin any longer, so that nothing worse may happen to you."
verses.5:15: The man went away and reported to the Jews that Jesus was the One who had made him well.
verses.5:16: And for this reason the Jews were persecuting Jesus, because He was doing these things on the Sabbath.
verses.5:17: But He answered them, "My Father is working until now, and I also am working."
verses.5:18: For this reason, therefore, the Jews were seeking all the more to kill Him, because He was not only breaking the Sabbath, but was also calling God His own Father, making Himself equal to God.
verses.5:19: So Jesus answered and said to them, "Truly, truly, I tell you, the Son can do nothing from Himself, unless He sees the Father doing something; for whatever He does, these things the Son also does in the same way.
verses.5:20: For the Father loves the Son and shows Him all the things that He Himself does; and He will show Him greater works than these, so that you may marvel.
verses.5:21: For just as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, so also the Son gives life to whom He wills.
verses.5:22: For not even the Father judges anyone, but He has given all judgment to the Son,
verses.5:23: so that all may honor the Son just as they honor the Father. The one who does not honor the Son does not honor the Father who sent Him.
verses.5:24: Truly, truly, I tell you, the one who hears My word and believes Him who sent Me has eternal life, and does not come into judgment, but has crossed over out of death into life.
verses.5:25: Truly, truly, I tell you, an hour is coming and is now here, when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God, and those who have heard will live.
verses.5:26: For just as the Father has life in Himself, so He also gave the Son to have life in Himself,
verses.5:27: and He gave Him authority to carry out judgment, because He is Son of Man.
verses.5:28: Do not marvel at this, because an hour is coming in which all who are in the tombs will hear His voice
verses.5:29: and will come out—those who did good things to a resurrection of life, and those who practiced evil things to a resurrection of judgment.
verses.5:30: I cannot do anything from Myself; just as I hear, I judge, and My judgment is righteous, because I do not seek My own will, but the will of the One who sent Me.
verses.5:31: If I testify about Myself, My testimony is not true.
verses.5:32: There is Another who testifies about Me, and I know that the testimony that He testifies about Me is true.
verses.5:33: You have sent to John, and he has testified to the truth.
verses.5:34: Yet I do not receive testimony from a man, but I say these things so that you may be saved.
verses.5:35: He was the burning and shining lamp, and you were willing to rejoice for an hour in his light.
verses.5:36: But I have testimony greater than that of John; for the works that the Father has given Me to complete, these very works that I do, testify about Me that the Father has sent Me.
verses.5:37: And the Father who sent Me, He Himself has testified about Me. You have neither heard His voice at any time nor seen His form,
verses.5:38: and you do not have His word remaining in you, because you do not believe the One whom He sent.
verses.5:39: You search the Scriptures because you suppose that in them you have eternal life; and those are the ones that testify about Me,
verses.5:40: yet you are unwilling to come to Me so that you may have life.
verses.5:41: I do not receive glory from people,
verses.5:42: but I know you, that you do not have the love of God in yourselves.
verses.5:43: I have come in the name of My Father, and you do not receive Me; if another comes in his own name, you will receive him.
verses.5:44: How are you able to believe, receiving glory from one another, while you do not seek the glory that comes from the only God?
verses.5:45: Do not suppose that I will accuse you before the Father; the one who accuses you is Moses, in whom you have placed your hope.
verses.5:46: For if you believed Moses, you would believe Me, for he wrote about Me.
verses.5:47: But if you do not believe his writings, how will you believe My words?"
verses.6:1: After these things Jesus departed to the other side of the Sea of Galilee, that of Tiberias.
verses.6:2: And a large crowd kept following Him, because they were observing the signs that He was performing on those who were sick.
verses.6:3: And Jesus went up onto the mountain, and He was sitting there with His disciples.
verses.6:4: Now the Passover, the festival of the Jews, was near.
verses.6:5: So Jesus, lifting up His eyes and seeing that a large crowd was coming toward Him, said to Philip, "Where should we buy bread so that these people may eat?"
verses.6:6: Now He was saying this, testing him, for He Himself knew what He was about to do.
verses.6:7: Philip answered Him, "Two hundred denarii worth of bread is not enough for them, so that each one may receive a small amount."
verses.6:8: One of His disciples, Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, said to Him,
verses.6:9: "There is a young boy here who has five barley loaves and two fish, but what are these among so many?"
verses.6:10: Jesus said, "Have the people recline." Now there was abundant grass in that place. So the men reclined, about five thousand in number.
verses.6:11: Jesus therefore took the loaves, and after giving thanks, He distributed them to those who were reclining; likewise also from the fish, as much as they wanted.
verses.6:12: And when they were filled, He said to His disciples, "Gather up the broken pieces that are left over, so that nothing may be lost."
verses.6:13: So they gathered them up and filled twelve baskets with broken pieces from the five barley loaves that were left over by those who had eaten.
verses.6:14: So when the people saw the sign that He had performed, they kept saying, "This is truly the Prophet who is coming into the world."
verses.6:15: Jesus, therefore, knowing that they were about to come and seize Him to make Him king, withdrew again to the mountain Himself alone.
verses.6:16: And when evening arrived, His disciples went down to the sea,
verses.6:17: and after boarding a boat, they were going across the sea to Capernaum. Darkness had already come, and Jesus had not yet come to them,
verses.6:18: and the sea was being stirred up as a strong wind was blowing.
verses.6:19: Then, when they had rowed about twenty-five or thirty stadia, they saw Jesus walking on the sea and coming near to the boat, and they became afraid.
verses.6:20: But He told them, "It is I; do not be afraid."
verses.6:21: So they wanted to take Him into the boat, and immediately the boat arrived at the land to which they were going.
verses.6:22: On the next day, the crowd that stood on the other side of the sea saw that no other small boat was there except one, and that Jesus had not entered the boat with His disciples, but His disciples had departed alone.
verses.6:23: Other small boats came from Tiberias near to the place where they had eaten the bread after the Lord had given thanks.
verses.6:24: Therefore, when the crowd saw that Jesus was not there, nor were His disciples, they themselves boarded the small boats and came to Capernaum, seeking Jesus.
verses.6:25: And having found Him on the other side of the sea, they said to Him, "Rabbi, when did You arrive here?"
verses.6:26: Jesus answered them and said, "Truly, truly, I tell you, you are seeking Me not because you saw signs, but because you ate from the loaves and were satisfied.
verses.6:27: Do not work for the food that perishes, but for the food that endures to eternal life, which the Son of Man will give you; for God the Father has placed His seal on Him."
verses.6:28: So they said to Him, "What must we do so that we may work the works of God?"
verses.6:29: Jesus answered and said to them, "This is the work of God: that you believe in Him whom He sent."
verses.6:30: Then they said to Him, "What sign, therefore, are You performing, so that we may see and believe You? What work are You doing?
verses.6:31: Our fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, just as it stands written, 'He gave them bread from heaven to eat.'"
verses.6:32: Therefore Jesus said to them, "Truly, truly, I tell you, it is not Moses who has given you the bread from heaven, but My Father is giving you the true bread from heaven.
verses.6:33: For the bread of God is that which descends from heaven and gives life to the world."
verses.6:34: So they said to Him, "Lord, give us this bread always."
verses.6:35: Jesus said to them, "I am the bread of life. The one who comes to Me will certainly not hunger, and the one who believes in Me will never thirst at any time.
verses.6:36: But I told you that you have indeed seen Me, and yet you do not believe.
verses.6:37: Everything that the Father gives Me will come to Me, and the one who comes to Me I will by no means cast out;
verses.6:38: for I have descended from heaven not to do My own will, but the will of Him who sent Me.
verses.6:39: And this is the will of Him who sent Me: that of everything He has given Me, I should lose nothing, but should raise it up on the last day.
verses.6:40: For this is the will of My Father: that everyone who sees the Son and believes in Him should have eternal life, and I Myself will raise him up on the last day."
verses.6:41: The Jews, therefore, were grumbling about Him because He said, "I am the bread that descended from heaven,"
verses.6:42: and they were saying, "Is this not Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? How does He now say, 'I have descended from heaven'?"
verses.6:43: Jesus answered and said to them, "Stop grumbling with one another.
verses.6:44: No one is able to come to Me unless the Father who sent Me draws him, and I Myself will raise him up on the last day.
verses.6:45: It stands written in the Prophets, 'And all of them will be taught by God.' Everyone who has heard from the Father and learned comes to Me.
verses.6:46: Not that anyone has seen the Father except the One who is from God; this One has seen the Father.
verses.6:47: Truly, truly, I tell you, the one who believes has eternal life.
verses.6:48: I am the bread of life.
verses.6:49: Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, and died.
verses.6:50: This is the bread descending from heaven, so that a person may eat from it and not die.
verses.6:51: I am the living bread that descended from heaven. If anyone eats from this bread, he will live forever; and indeed the bread that I will give is My flesh, for the life of the world."
verses.6:52: So the Jews were quarreling with one another, saying, "How is this man able to give us His flesh to eat?"
verses.6:53: Therefore Jesus said to them, "Truly, truly, I tell you, unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink His blood, you do not have life in yourselves.
verses.6:54: The one who eats My flesh and drinks My blood has eternal life, and I Myself will raise him up on the last day.
verses.6:55: For My flesh is genuine food, and My blood is genuine drink.
verses.6:56: The one who eats My flesh and drinks My blood remains in Me, and I in him.
verses.6:57: Just as the living Father sent Me, and I live because of the Father, so the one who eats Me will also live because of Me.
verses.6:58: This is the bread that descended from heaven—not as the fathers ate and died; the one who eats this bread will live forever."
verses.6:59: He said these things while teaching in a synagogue in Capernaum.
verses.6:60: Therefore, when many of His disciples heard this, they said, "This saying is hard; who is able to listen to it?"
verses.6:61: But Jesus, knowing within Himself that His disciples were grumbling about this, said to them, "Does this cause you to stumble?
verses.6:62: What if, then, you should see the Son of Man ascending where He was before?
verses.6:63: The Spirit is the One who gives life; the flesh is of no benefit at all. The words that I have spoken to you are spirit and are life.
verses.6:64: Yet there are some among you who do not believe." For from the beginning Jesus knew who the ones were who did not believe, and who it was that would betray Him.
verses.6:65: And He was saying, "For this reason I have told you that no one is able to come to Me unless it has been given to him from the Father."
verses.6:66: Because of this, many of His disciples went back and were no longer walking with Him.
verses.6:67: Therefore Jesus said to the Twelve, "You do not also want to leave, do you?"
verses.6:68: Simon Peter answered Him, "Lord, to whom will we go? You have words of eternal life,
verses.6:69: and we ourselves have believed and come to know that You are the Holy One of God."
verses.6:70: Jesus answered them, "Did I Myself not choose you, the Twelve? Yet one from among you is a devil."
verses.6:71: Now He was speaking of Judas, son of Simon Iscariot, for he was about to betray Him—one of the Twelve.
verses.7:1: And after these things Jesus was walking in Galilee, for He did not want to walk in Judea, because the Jews were seeking to kill Him.
verses.7:2: Now the feast of the Jews, the Feast of Booths, was near.
verses.7:3: Therefore His brothers said to Him, "Depart from here and go into Judea, so that Your disciples also will see Your works that You are doing.
verses.7:4: For no one does anything in secret and seeks himself to be in public. If You do these things, reveal Yourself to the world."
verses.7:5: For not even His brothers were believing in Him.
verses.7:6: Therefore Jesus said to them, "My time is not yet here, but your time is always ready.
verses.7:7: The world cannot hate you, but it hates Me, because I testify about it that its works are evil.
verses.7:8: You go up to the feast; I am not yet going up to this feast, because My time has not yet been fulfilled."
verses.7:9: And having said these things to them, He remained in Galilee.
verses.7:10: But when His brothers went up to the feast, then He Himself also went up, not openly, but as though in secret.
verses.7:11: Therefore the Jews were seeking Him at the feast and were saying, "Where is that man?"
verses.7:12: And there was much muttering about Him among the crowds; some were saying, "He is good," while others were saying, "No, instead He is leading the crowd astray."
verses.7:13: Yet no one was speaking openly about Him because of the fear of the Jews.
verses.7:14: Now when the feast was already halfway through, Jesus went up into the temple and was teaching.
verses.7:15: Therefore the Jews were marveling, saying, "How does this man know letters, without having studied?"
verses.7:16: So Jesus answered them and said, "My teaching is not My own, but belongs to the One who sent Me.
verses.7:17: If anyone wants to do His will, he will know about the teaching, whether it is from God or whether I am speaking from Myself.
verses.7:18: The one who speaks from himself seeks his own glory; but the one who seeks the glory of the one who sent him, this one is true, and there is no unrighteousness in him.
verses.7:19: Has not Moses given you the law? Yet none of you keeps the law. Why are you seeking to kill Me?"
verses.7:20: The crowd answered, "You have a demon! Who is seeking to kill You?"
verses.7:21: Jesus answered and said to them, "I did one work, and you all marvel.
verses.7:22: Because of this, Moses has given you circumcision—not that it is from Moses, but from the fathers—and on a Sabbath you circumcise a man.
verses.7:23: If a man receives circumcision on a Sabbath so that the law of Moses will not be broken, are you angry with Me because I made a whole man well on a Sabbath?
verses.7:24: Do not judge according to appearance, but judge with righteous judgment."
verses.7:25: Therefore some of the people of Jerusalem were saying, "Is this not the man whom they are seeking to kill?
verses.7:26: And look, He is speaking openly, and they say nothing to Him! Could it be that the rulers have truly come to know that this man is the Christ?
verses.7:27: Yet we know where this man is from; but whenever the Christ comes, no one knows where He is from."
verses.7:28: Therefore Jesus cried out while teaching in the temple, saying, "You both know Me and know where I am from; and I have not come from Myself, but the One who sent Me is true, whom you do not know.
verses.7:29: I know Him, because I am from Him, and He sent Me."
verses.7:30: So they were seeking to seize Him, and no one laid a hand on Him, because His hour had not yet come.
verses.7:31: Yet many from the crowd believed in Him, and they were saying, "When the Christ comes, He will not perform more signs than what this man performed, will He?"
verses.7:32: The Pharisees heard the crowd muttering these things about Him, and the chief priests and the Pharisees sent officers to seize Him.
verses.7:33: Therefore Jesus said, "For a little while longer I am with you, and I am going to the One who sent Me.
verses.7:34: You will seek Me and will not find Me, and where I am, you cannot come."
verses.7:35: Therefore the Jews said to one another, "Where is this man about to go that we will not find Him? He is not about to go to the Dispersion among the Greeks and teach the Greeks, is He?
verses.7:36: What is this saying that He spoke: 'You will seek Me and will not find Me, and where I am, you cannot come'?"
verses.7:37: Now on the last day, the great day of the feast, Jesus was standing and cried out, saying, "If anyone is thirsty, let him come to Me and drink.
verses.7:38: The one who believes in Me, just as the Scripture said, rivers of living water will flow from his inner being."
verses.7:39: Now He said this about the Spirit, whom those who believed in Him were about to receive; for the Spirit was not yet, because Jesus had not yet been glorified.
verses.7:40: Therefore some of the crowd, when they heard these words, were saying, "This man is truly the Prophet."
verses.7:41: Others were saying, "This man is the Christ." Still others were saying, "Surely the Christ does not come from Galilee, does He?
verses.7:42: Has not the Scripture said that the Christ comes from the offspring of David, and from Bethlehem, the village where David was?"
verses.7:43: So a division occurred in the crowd because of Him.
verses.7:44: And some of them wanted to seize Him, but no one laid hands on Him.
verses.7:45: Therefore the officers came to the chief priests and Pharisees, and those men said to them, "Why did you not bring Him?"
verses.7:46: The officers answered, "Never has a man spoken like this."
verses.7:47: Therefore the Pharisees answered them, "You have not also been led astray, have you?
verses.7:48: Has any one of the rulers or of the Pharisees believed in Him?
verses.7:49: But this crowd that does not know the law is accursed."
verses.7:50: Nicodemus, the one who had come to Him earlier, being one of them, said to them,
verses.7:51: "Our law does not judge a man unless it first hears from him and knows what he is doing, does it?"
verses.7:52: They answered and said to him, "You are not also from Galilee, are you? Search and see that no prophet arises from Galilee."
verses.7:53: ⟦And each one went to his own house.⟧
verses.8:1: ⟦But Jesus went to the Mount of Olives.⟧
verses.8:2: ⟦And at dawn He came again into the temple, and all the people were coming; and having sat down, He began teaching them.⟧
verses.8:3: ⟦Now the scribes and the Pharisees bring to Him a woman caught in adultery; and having set her in the middle,⟧
verses.8:4: ⟦they say to Him, testing Him, "Teacher, this woman was caught in the very act of committing adultery.⟧
verses.8:5: ⟦Now in the law Moses commanded us to stone such women; what then do You say?"⟧
verses.8:6: ⟦Now they were saying this to test Him, so that they might have grounds to accuse Him. But Jesus, bending down, was writing with His finger on the ground, acting as though He did not notice.⟧
verses.8:7: ⟦Yet as they persisted in questioning Him, He straightened up and said to them, "Let the one among you who is without sin throw the stone at her first."⟧
verses.8:8: ⟦And bending down again, He was writing on the ground.⟧
verses.8:9: ⟦Now they, when they heard it and were convicted by their conscience, began going out one by one, starting from the elders; and Jesus alone was left, and the woman who was in the middle.⟧
verses.8:10: ⟦Then Jesus straightened up and, seeing no one except the woman, said to her, "Where are those accusers of yours? Did no one condemn you?"⟧
verses.8:11: ⟦And she said, "No one, Lord." And Jesus said, "Neither do I judge you; go, and sin no more."⟧
verses.8:12: So Jesus spoke to them again, saying, "I am the light of the world. The one who follows Me will never walk in the darkness, but will have the light of life."
verses.8:13: Therefore the Pharisees said to Him, "You testify concerning Yourself; Your testimony is not true."
verses.8:14: Jesus replied and said to them, "Even if I testify concerning Myself, My testimony is true, because I know where I came from and where I am going; yet you do not know where I come from or where I am going.
verses.8:15: You judge according to the flesh; I do not judge anyone.
verses.8:16: And even if I do judge, My judgment is genuine, because I am not alone, but it is I and the Father who sent Me.
verses.8:17: And in your own law also it is written that the testimony of two people is true.
verses.8:18: I am the One testifying concerning Myself, and the Father who sent Me testifies concerning Me."
verses.8:19: Therefore they were saying to Him, "Where is Your Father?" Jesus replied, "You know neither Me nor My Father; if you knew Me, you would know My Father as well."
verses.8:20: He spoke these words in the treasury while teaching in the temple, and no one seized Him, because His hour had not yet arrived.
verses.8:21: So He said to them again, "I am going away, and you will seek Me, and you will die in your sin. Where I am going, you are not able to come."
verses.8:22: Therefore the Jews were saying, "He will not kill Himself, will He, since He says, 'Where I am going, you are not able to come'?"
verses.8:23: And He was saying to them, "You are from below; I am from above. You are from this world; I am not from this world.
verses.8:24: Therefore I told you that you will die in your sins; for unless you believe that I am, you will die in your sins."
verses.8:25: Therefore they were saying to Him, "Who are You?" Jesus said to them, "Why am I even speaking to you at all?
verses.8:26: I have many things to speak and to judge concerning you, yet the One who sent Me is true, and the things I heard from Him, these I speak to the world."
verses.8:27: They did not realize that He was telling them about the Father.
verses.8:28: So Jesus said to them, "When you lift up the Son of Man, then you will know that I am, and I do nothing on My own, but just as the Father taught Me, these things I speak.
verses.8:29: And the One who sent Me is with Me. He has not left Me alone, because I do the things pleasing to Him at all times."
verses.8:30: While He was speaking these things, many believed in Him.
verses.8:31: Therefore Jesus was saying to the Jews who had believed Him, "If you remain in My word, you are truly disciples of Mine,
verses.8:32: and you will know the truth, and the truth will free you."
verses.8:33: They answered Him, "We are offspring of Abraham and have never been enslaved to anyone. How do You say, 'You will become free'?"
verses.8:34: Jesus replied to them, "Truly, truly, I tell you that everyone who commits sin is a slave of sin.
verses.8:35: Now the slave does not remain in the house forever; the son remains forever.
verses.8:36: Therefore, if the Son frees you, you will really be free.
verses.8:37: I know that you are offspring of Abraham; yet you seek to kill Me, because My word has no room in you.
verses.8:38: I speak the things that I have seen with the Father; and so you also do the things that you heard from the father."
verses.8:39: They answered and said to Him, "Abraham is our father." Jesus said to them, "If you are children of Abraham, you would be doing the works of Abraham;
verses.8:40: but now you seek to kill Me, a man who has spoken to you the truth that I heard from God. Abraham did not do this.
verses.8:41: You are doing the works of your father." They said to Him, "We were not born out of sexual immorality; we have one Father, God."
verses.8:42: Jesus said to them, "If God were your Father, you would love Me, for I came forth from God and am here; for I have not even come on My own, but He sent Me.
verses.8:43: Why do you not understand My speech? Because you are not able to hear My word.
verses.8:44: You are from your father the devil, and you want to do the desires of your father. He was a murderer from the beginning and did not stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him. Whenever he speaks a lie, he speaks from what is his own, because he is a liar and the father of it.
verses.8:45: Yet as for Me, because I tell the truth, you do not believe Me.
verses.8:46: Who among you convicts Me of sin? If I tell the truth, why do you not believe Me?
verses.8:47: The one who is from God hears the words of God; for this reason you do not hear, because you are not from God."
verses.8:48: The Jews replied and said to Him, "Do we not rightly say that You are a Samaritan and have a demon?"
verses.8:49: Jesus replied, "I do not have a demon; rather, I honor My Father, yet you dishonor Me.
verses.8:50: I, however, do not seek My own glory; there is One who seeks and judges.
verses.8:51: Truly, truly, I tell you, if anyone keeps My word, he will never see death."
verses.8:52: The Jews said to Him, "Now we know that You have a demon. Abraham died, and the prophets as well, yet You say, 'If anyone keeps My word, he will never taste death.'
verses.8:53: You are not greater than our father Abraham, who died, are You? And the prophets died too. Who do You make Yourself out to be?"
verses.8:54: Jesus replied, "If I glorify Myself, My glory is nothing; it is My Father who glorifies Me, of whom you say, 'He is our God,'
verses.8:55: and you have not known Him, yet I know Him. And if I say that I do not know Him, I will be a liar like you; but I do know Him, and I keep His word.
verses.8:56: Abraham your father exulted that he would see My day, and he saw it and was glad."
verses.8:57: Therefore the Jews said to Him, "You are not yet fifty years old, and You have seen Abraham?"
verses.8:58: Jesus said to them, "Truly, truly, I tell you, before Abraham came into being, I am."
verses.8:59: So they picked up stones to throw at Him, yet Jesus concealed Himself and went out from the temple.
verses.9:1: And passing along, He saw a man blind from birth.
verses.9:2: And His disciples questioned Him, saying, "Rabbi, who sinned, this man or his parents, so that he would be born blind?"
verses.9:3: Jesus answered, "Neither this man nor his parents sinned, but it was so that the works of God would be revealed in him.
verses.9:4: It is necessary for us to work the works of the One who sent Me while it is day; night is coming when no one is able to work.
verses.9:5: For as long as I am in the world, I am the light of the world."
verses.9:6: Having said these things, He spat on the ground, made mud from the saliva, and spread the mud on his eyes,
verses.9:7: and said to him, "Go, wash in the pool of Siloam" (which is translated "Sent"). So he went away, washed, and returned seeing.
verses.9:8: Therefore the neighbors and those who had previously seen him as a beggar were saying, "Is this not the one who used to sit and beg?"
verses.9:9: Some were saying, "This is he." Others were saying, "No, but he is like him." He himself was saying, "I am he."
verses.9:10: So they were saying to him, "How were your eyes opened?"
verses.9:11: He answered, "The man who is called Jesus made mud and spread it on my eyes, and said to me, 'Go to Siloam and wash.' So I went away and washed, and I received sight."
verses.9:12: And they said to him, "Where is He?" He said, "I do not know."
verses.9:13: They brought him to the Pharisees, the one who was formerly blind.
verses.9:14: Now it was a Sabbath on the day when Jesus made the mud and opened his eyes.
verses.9:15: So again the Pharisees also were questioning him as to how he received sight. And he said to them, "He put mud on my eyes, and I washed, and I see."
verses.9:16: Therefore some of the Pharisees were saying, "This man is not from God, because He does not keep the Sabbath." Others were saying, "How is a sinful man able to perform such signs?" And there was a division among them.
verses.9:17: Therefore they said again to the blind man, "What do you yourself say concerning Him, seeing that He opened your eyes?" And he replied, "He is a prophet."
verses.9:18: Therefore the Jews did not believe concerning him that he had been blind and had received sight, until they called the parents of him who had received sight
verses.9:19: and questioned them, saying, "Is this your son, whom you say was born blind? How then does he now see?"
verses.9:20: His parents therefore answered and said, "We know that this is our son, and that he was born blind;
verses.9:21: but how he now sees we do not know, or who opened his eyes we ourselves do not know. Ask him; he is of age; he himself will speak for himself."
verses.9:22: His parents said these things because they were afraid of the Jews; for the Jews had already agreed that if anyone confessed Him as Christ, he should be put out of the synagogue.
verses.9:23: For this reason his parents said, "He is of age; question him."
verses.9:24: So a second time they called the man who had been blind and said to him, "Give glory to God; we know that this man is a sinner."
verses.9:25: He therefore answered, "Whether He is a sinner, I do not know; one thing I know, that although I was blind, I now see."
verses.9:26: So they said to him, "What did He do to you? How did He open your eyes?"
verses.9:27: He answered them, "I already told you, and you did not listen. Why do you want to hear it again? You do not also want to become His disciples, do you?"
verses.9:28: And they reviled him and said, "You are a disciple of that man, but we are disciples of Moses.
verses.9:29: We know that God has spoken to Moses, but as for this man, we do not know where He is from."
verses.9:30: The man answered and said to them, "Indeed, this is the astonishing thing: you do not know where He is from, and yet He opened my eyes.
verses.9:31: We know that God does not listen to sinners, but if anyone is God-fearing and does His will, He listens to that one.
verses.9:32: From the beginning of time it has never been heard that anyone opened the eyes of a person born blind.
verses.9:33: If this man were not from God, He would be unable to do anything."
verses.9:34: They answered and said to him, "You were born completely in sins, and are you teaching us?" And they threw him out.
verses.9:35: Jesus heard that they had thrown him out, and having found him, He said, "Do you believe in the Son of Man?"
verses.9:36: He answered and said, "And who is He, sir, so that I may believe in Him?"
verses.9:37: Jesus said to him, "You have both seen Him, and the One who is speaking with you is He."
verses.9:38: And he said, "I believe, Lord." And he worshiped Him.
verses.9:39: And Jesus said, "For judgment I Myself came into this world, so that those who do not see may see, and those who see may become blind."
verses.9:40: Those of the Pharisees who were with Him heard these things and said to Him, "We are not also blind, are we?"
verses.9:41: Jesus said to them, "If you were blind, you would not have sin; but as it is, you say, 'We see.' Your sin remains."
verses.10:1: "Truly, truly, I tell you, the one who does not enter through the door into the fold of the sheep, but climbs up from another place, that one is a thief and a bandit.
verses.10:2: But the one who enters through the door is a shepherd of the sheep.
verses.10:3: To this one the doorkeeper opens, and the sheep listen to his voice; and he calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.
verses.10:4: Whenever he has brought out all his own, he goes ahead of them, and the sheep follow him, because they know his voice.
verses.10:5: Yet a stranger they will certainly not follow, but will flee from him, because they do not know the voice of strangers."
verses.10:6: This figure of speech Jesus spoke to them, yet they did not understand what the things were that He was speaking to them.
verses.10:7: Therefore Jesus said to them again, "Truly, truly, I tell you, I am the door of the sheep.
verses.10:8: All who came before Me are thieves and bandits, but the sheep did not listen to them.
verses.10:9: I am the door; if anyone enters through Me, he will be saved, and will go in and go out and find pasture.
verses.10:10: The thief does not come except to steal and slaughter and destroy; I came so that they may have life and have it in abundance.
verses.10:11: I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down His life on behalf of the sheep.
verses.10:12: The hired worker, who is not a shepherd and to whom the sheep do not belong, sees the wolf coming and abandons the sheep and flees—and the wolf snatches them and scatters them—
verses.10:13: because he is a hired worker and does not care about the sheep.
verses.10:14: I am the good shepherd, and I know My own and My own know Me,
verses.10:15: just as the Father knows Me and I know the Father; and I lay down My life on behalf of the sheep.
verses.10:16: And I have other sheep that are not from this fold; those also I must bring, and they will listen to My voice, and they will become one flock, one shepherd.
verses.10:17: For this reason the Father loves Me, because I lay down My life so that I may take it up again.
verses.10:18: No one has taken it from Me, but I lay it down of Myself. I have authority to lay it down, and I have authority to take it up again. This command I received from My Father."
verses.10:19: A division occurred again among the Jews because of these words.
verses.10:20: And many of them were saying, "He has a demon and is out of His mind; why do you listen to Him?"
verses.10:21: Others were saying, "These sayings are not those of someone demon-possessed. A demon cannot open the eyes of the blind, can it?"
verses.10:22: Then the Feast of Dedication took place in Jerusalem; it was winter,
verses.10:23: and Jesus was walking in the temple, in the colonnade of Solomon.
verses.10:24: Therefore the Jews surrounded Him and were saying to Him, "How long will You keep us in suspense? If You are the Christ, tell us plainly."
verses.10:25: Jesus answered them, "I told you, and you do not believe. The works that I do in the name of My Father, these testify about Me.
verses.10:26: But you do not believe, because you are not among My sheep.
verses.10:27: My sheep listen to My voice, and I know them, and they follow Me,
verses.10:28: and I give them eternal life, and they will certainly never perish, and no one will snatch them from My hand.
verses.10:29: What My Father has given Me is greater than all, and no one is able to snatch them from the Father's hand.
verses.10:30: I and the Father are one."
verses.10:31: The Jews picked up stones again in order to stone Him.
verses.10:32: Jesus answered them, "I have shown you many good works from the Father; for which of these works are you stoning Me?"
verses.10:33: The Jews answered Him, "We are not stoning You for a good work, but for blasphemy, and because You, being a man, make Yourself God."
verses.10:34: Jesus answered them, "Is it not written in your law, 'I said, you are gods'?
verses.10:35: If He called those gods to whom the word of God came—and the Scripture cannot be broken—
verses.10:36: do you say of Him whom the Father consecrated and sent into the world, 'You are blaspheming,' because I said, 'I am the Son of God'?
verses.10:37: If I am not doing the works of My Father, do not believe Me;
verses.10:38: but if I am doing them, even if you do not believe Me, believe the works, so that you may come to know and continue knowing that the Father is in Me, and I am in the Father."
verses.10:39: Therefore they were seeking again to seize Him, and He escaped from their hand.
verses.10:40: And He went away again across the Jordan to the place where John was at first baptizing, and He remained there.
verses.10:41: And many came to Him and were saying, "John performed no sign, yet everything that John said about this Man was true."
verses.10:42: And many believed in Him there.
verses.11:1: Now a certain man was ill, Lazarus from Bethany, of the village of Mary and Martha her sister.
verses.11:2: And it was Mary who anointed the Lord with perfumed oil and wiped His feet with her hair, whose brother Lazarus was ill.
verses.11:3: So the sisters sent to Him, saying, "Lord, look, the one You love is ill."
verses.11:4: When Jesus heard it, He said, "This illness does not lead to death, but is for the glory of God, so that the Son of God may be glorified through it."
verses.11:5: And Jesus loved Martha, her sister, and Lazarus.
verses.11:6: So when He heard that he was ill, He then stayed in the place where He was for two days.
verses.11:7: Then after this He said to the disciples, "Let us go to Judea again."
verses.11:8: The disciples said to Him, "Rabbi, the Jews were just now seeking to stone You, and are You going there again?"
verses.11:9: Jesus answered, "Are there not twelve hours in the day? If anyone walks in the day, he does not stumble, because he sees the light of this world.
verses.11:10: But if anyone walks in the night, he stumbles, because the light is not in him."
verses.11:11: He said these things, and after this He said to them, "Our friend Lazarus has fallen asleep, but I am going so that I may wake him up."
verses.11:12: The disciples therefore said to Him, "Lord, if he has fallen asleep, he will recover."
verses.11:13: Now Jesus had spoken of his death, whereas they supposed that He was speaking about resting in sleep.
verses.11:14: So then Jesus told them plainly, "Lazarus has died,
verses.11:15: and I rejoice for your sake that I was not there, so that you may believe; but let us go to him."
verses.11:16: Therefore Thomas, who is called Didymus, said to his fellow disciples, "Let us also go, so that we may die with Him."
verses.11:17: So when Jesus arrived, He found that he had already been in the tomb for four days.
verses.11:18: Now Bethany was near Jerusalem, about fifteen stadia away.
verses.11:19: And many of the Jews had come to Martha and Mary in order to console them concerning their brother.
verses.11:20: Therefore Martha, when she heard that Jesus was coming, went to meet Him, while Mary was sitting in the house.
verses.11:21: Martha then said to Jesus, "Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died.
verses.11:22: And even now I know that whatever You ask from God, God will give You."
verses.11:23: Jesus said to her, "Your brother will rise."
verses.11:24: Martha said to Him, "I know that he will rise in the resurrection on the last day."
verses.11:25: Jesus said to her, "I am the resurrection and the life. The one who believes in Me, even if he dies, will live,
verses.11:26: and everyone who lives and believes in Me will by no means ever die. Do you believe this?"
verses.11:27: She said to Him, "Yes, Lord; I have come to believe that You are the Christ, the Son of God, the One coming into the world."
verses.11:28: And having said this, she went away and called Mary her sister secretly, saying, "The Teacher is here and is calling you."
verses.11:29: And when she heard it, she got up quickly and was coming to Him.
verses.11:30: Now Jesus had not yet come into the village, but was still at the place where Martha had met Him.
verses.11:31: Therefore the Jews who were with her in the house and consoling her, when they saw that Mary got up quickly and went out, followed her, supposing that she was going to the tomb in order to weep there.
verses.11:32: So when Mary came to where Jesus was and saw Him, she fell at His feet, saying to Him, "Lord, if You had been here, my brother would not have died."
verses.11:33: Therefore when Jesus saw her weeping, and the Jews who had come with her weeping, He was deeply stirred in spirit and troubled Himself,
verses.11:34: and said, "Where have you laid him?" They said to Him, "Lord, come and see."
verses.11:36: So the Jews were saying, "Look how He loved him!"
verses.11:37: But some of them said, "Could not this man, who opened the eyes of the blind man, have made it so that this man also would not die?"
verses.11:38: Jesus therefore, again deeply stirred within Himself, came to the tomb. Now it was a cave, and a stone lay against it.
verses.11:39: Jesus said, "Remove the stone." Martha, the sister of the one who had died, said to Him, "Lord, already there is a stench, for it is the fourth day."
verses.11:40: Jesus said to her, "Did I not tell you that if you believe, you will see the glory of God?"
verses.11:41: So they removed the stone. And Jesus lifted His eyes upward and said, "Father, I thank You that You heard Me.
verses.11:42: And I knew that You always hear Me; yet because of the crowd standing around I said it, so that they may believe that You sent Me."
verses.11:43: And when He had said these things, He cried out with a loud voice, "Lazarus, come out here!"
verses.11:44: The one who had died came out, with his feet and hands bound in burial strips, and his face was wrapped around with a cloth. Jesus said to them, "Unbind him and let him go."
verses.11:45: Therefore many of the Jews who had come to Mary and seen the things He did believed in Him;
verses.11:46: but some of them went away to the Pharisees and told them the things Jesus had done.
verses.11:47: Therefore the chief priests and the Pharisees convened a council and were saying, "What are we doing, since this man is performing many signs?
verses.11:48: If we let Him go on like this, everyone will believe in Him, and the Romans will come and take away both our place and our nation."
verses.11:49: But a certain one of them, Caiaphas, being high priest that year, said to them, "You know nothing at all,
verses.11:50: nor do you consider that it is advantageous for you that one man die on behalf of the people, and that the whole nation not perish."
verses.11:51: Now he did not say this on his own, but being high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus was going to die on behalf of the nation,
verses.11:52: and not on behalf of the nation only, but so that He might also gather together into one the scattered children of God.
verses.11:53: So from that day on they planned together to kill Him.
verses.11:54: Therefore Jesus no longer walked openly among the Jews, but went away from there to the region near the wilderness, to a city called Ephraim, and there He stayed with the disciples.
verses.11:55: Now the Passover of the Jews was near, and many went up to Jerusalem from the countryside before the Passover in order to purify themselves.
verses.11:56: So they were seeking Jesus and saying to one another as they stood in the temple, "What do you think? That He will not come to the festival at all?"
verses.11:57: Now the chief priests and the Pharisees had given orders that if anyone knew where He was, he should report it, so that they might seize Him.
verses.12:1: Therefore, six days before the Passover, Jesus came to Bethany, where Lazarus was, whom Jesus had raised from the dead.
verses.12:2: So they made a dinner for Him there, and Martha was serving, while Lazarus was one of those reclining at table with Him.
verses.12:3: Then Mary, taking a pound of very costly ointment of genuine nard, anointed the feet of Jesus and wiped His feet with her hair; and the house was filled with the fragrance of the ointment.
verses.12:4: But Judas Iscariot, one of His disciples, the one who was about to betray Him, said,
verses.12:5: "Why was this ointment not sold for three hundred denarii and given to the poor?"
verses.12:6: Now he said this, not because he cared about the poor, but because he was a thief, and since he held the money box, he used to take what was put into it.
verses.12:7: Therefore Jesus said, "Leave her alone, so that she may keep it for the day of My burial;
verses.12:8: for the poor you always have with you, but you do not always have Me."
verses.12:9: Then a large crowd of the Jews learned that He was there, and they came not because of Jesus alone, but so that they might also see Lazarus, whom He had raised from the dead.
verses.12:10: But the chief priests plotted to kill Lazarus as well,
verses.12:11: because on account of him many of the Jews were going away and believing in Jesus.
verses.12:12: On the next day, the large crowd that had come to the feast, hearing that Jesus was coming to Jerusalem,
verses.12:13: took the branches of the palm trees and went out to meet Him, and they were shouting, "Hosanna! Blessed is the One coming in the name of the Lord, even the King of Israel!"
verses.12:14: And Jesus, having found a young donkey, sat on it, just as it is written:
verses.12:15: "Do not fear, daughter of Zion; look, your King is coming, seated on a donkey's colt."
verses.12:16: His disciples did not understand these things at first, but when Jesus was glorified, then they remembered that these things had been written about Him and that they had done these things to Him.
verses.12:17: So the crowd that was with Him when He called Lazarus out of the tomb and raised him from the dead kept testifying.
verses.12:18: For this reason also the crowd went to meet Him, because they heard that He had performed this sign.
verses.12:19: Therefore the Pharisees said to one another, "You see that you are gaining nothing; look, the world has gone after Him!"
verses.12:20: Now there were some Greeks among those who were going up to worship at the feast.
verses.12:21: So these approached Philip, who was from Bethsaida of Galilee, and were asking him, saying, "Sir, we want to see Jesus."
verses.12:22: Philip came and told Andrew; Andrew and Philip came and told Jesus.
verses.12:23: And Jesus answered them, saying, "The hour has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.
verses.12:24: Truly, truly, I say to you, unless the grain of wheat falls into the earth and dies, it remains by itself alone; but if it dies, it bears much fruit.
verses.12:25: The one who loves his life loses it, and the one who hates his life in this world will keep it for eternal life.
verses.12:26: If anyone serves Me, let him follow Me; and where I am, there My servant will also be. If anyone serves Me, the Father will honor him.
verses.12:27: Now My soul is troubled, and what shall I say? Father, save Me from this hour. Yet for this reason I came to this hour.
verses.12:28: Father, glorify Your name." Then a voice came out of heaven: "I have both glorified it, and I will glorify it again."
verses.12:29: So the crowd that was standing by and heard it was saying that it had thundered; others were saying, "An angel has spoken to Him."
verses.12:30: Jesus answered and said, "This voice has not come for My sake, but for your sake.
verses.12:31: Now is the judgment of this world; now the ruler of this world will be cast out.
verses.12:32: And I, if I am lifted up from the earth, will draw all people to Myself."
verses.12:33: Now He was saying this to indicate by what kind of death He was about to die.
verses.12:34: Therefore the crowd answered Him, "We have heard from the Law that the Christ remains forever, and how do You say that the Son of Man must be lifted up? Who is this Son of Man?"
verses.12:35: So Jesus said to them, "For a little while longer the light is among you. Walk while you have the light, so that darkness may not overtake you; and the one who walks in the darkness does not know where he is going.
verses.12:36: While you have the light, believe in the light, so that you may become sons of light." Jesus spoke these things, and going away, He hid Himself from them.
verses.12:37: Yet although He had performed so many signs before them, they were not believing in Him,
verses.12:38: so that the word of Isaiah the prophet might be fulfilled, which he spoke: "Lord, who has believed our report? And to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?"
verses.12:39: For this reason they were not able to believe, because Isaiah said again:
verses.12:40: "He has blinded their eyes and hardened their heart, so that they would not see with their eyes and understand with their heart and turn, and I would heal them."
verses.12:41: Isaiah said these things because he saw His glory, and he spoke about Him.
verses.12:42: Yet even so, many even among the rulers believed in Him, but because of the Pharisees they were not confessing it, so that they would not be put out of the synagogue;
verses.12:43: for they loved the glory of people more than the glory of God.
verses.12:44: Then Jesus cried out and said, "The one who believes in Me does not believe in Me, but in the One who sent Me;
verses.12:45: and the one who sees Me sees the One who sent Me.
verses.12:46: I have come as light into the world, so that everyone who believes in Me may not remain in the darkness.
verses.12:47: And if anyone hears My words and does not keep them, I do not judge him; for I did not come to judge the world, but to save the world.
verses.12:48: The one who rejects Me and does not receive My words has one who judges him: the word that I spoke, that will judge him on the last day.
verses.12:49: For I did not speak from Myself, but the Father who sent Me has Himself given Me a command as to what to say and what to speak.
verses.12:50: And I know that His command is eternal life. Therefore, the things that I speak, just as the Father has told Me, so I speak."
verses.13:1: Now before the festival of the Passover, knowing that His hour had come that He should depart from this world to the Father, Jesus, having loved His own who were in the world, loved them to the end.
verses.13:2: And while supper was underway, the devil having already put into the heart that Judas Iscariot, son of Simon, should betray Him,
verses.13:3: knowing that the Father had given all things into His hands, and that He had come out from God and was going to God,
verses.13:4: He got up from supper and laid aside His outer garments, and taking a towel, wrapped it around Himself.
verses.13:5: Then He poured water into the basin and began to wash the feet of the disciples and to wipe them with the towel that was wrapped around Him.
verses.13:6: So He came to Simon Peter, and he said to Him, "Lord, are You washing my feet?"
verses.13:7: Jesus answered and said to him, "What I am doing you do not know now, but you will understand after these things."
verses.13:8: Peter said to Him, "You will never wash my feet!" Jesus answered him, "If I do not wash you, you have no share with Me."
verses.13:9: Simon Peter said to Him, "Lord, not my feet only, but also my hands and my head!"
verses.13:10: Jesus said to him, "The one who has bathed has no need except to wash his feet, but is completely clean; and you are clean, yet not all of you."
verses.13:11: For He knew the one who was betraying Him; because of this He said, "Not all of you are clean."
verses.13:12: So when He had washed their feet and taken His outer garments and reclined at table, He said to them again, "Do you know what I have done for you?
verses.13:13: You call Me 'Teacher' and 'Lord,' and you speak rightly, for I am.
verses.13:14: If then I, the Lord and the Teacher, washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another's feet.
verses.13:15: For I have given you an example, so that just as I did for you, you also should do.
verses.13:16: Truly, truly, I tell you, a slave is not greater than his master, nor is a messenger greater than the one who sent him.
verses.13:17: If you know these things, blessed are you if you do them.
verses.13:18: I am not speaking about all of you; I know whom I have chosen—but so that the Scripture may be fulfilled: 'The one who eats bread with Me has lifted up his heel against Me.'
verses.13:19: From now on I am telling you before it happens, so that when it happens you may believe that I am.
verses.13:20: Truly, truly, I tell you, whoever receives anyone I send receives Me, and the one who receives Me receives the One who sent Me."
verses.13:21: Having said these things, Jesus was troubled in spirit, and He testified and said, "Truly, truly, I tell you that one of you will betray Me."
verses.13:22: The disciples were looking at one another, perplexed as to whom He was speaking about.
verses.13:23: Now one of His disciples, whom Jesus loved, was reclining close to Jesus's chest.
verses.13:24: So Simon Peter signaled to him to ask who it might be about whom He was speaking.
verses.13:25: Leaning back like that against Jesus's chest, he said to Him, "Lord, who is it?"
verses.13:26: Jesus answered, "It is the one to whom I will give the morsel once I dip it." So after dipping the morsel, He gave it to Judas, son of Simon Iscariot.
verses.13:27: And after the morsel, Satan then entered into him. So Jesus said to him, "What you are doing, do quickly."
verses.13:28: Now no one of those reclining at table understood why He said this to him.
verses.13:29: For some were supposing, since Judas kept the money box, that Jesus was saying to him, "Buy what we need for the festival," or that he should give something to the poor.
verses.13:30: So after taking the morsel, he went out immediately. And it was night.
verses.13:31: Therefore, when he had gone out, Jesus said, "Now the Son of Man has been glorified, and God has been glorified in Him;
verses.13:32: and God will glorify Him in Himself, and will glorify Him at once.
verses.13:33: Little children, I am with you a little while longer. You will seek Me, and just as I said to the Jews, 'Where I am going you cannot come,' I now tell you as well.
verses.13:34: I am giving you a new commandment, that you love one another; just as I loved you, that you also should love one another.
verses.13:35: By this everyone will know that you are My disciples, if you have love among one another."
verses.13:36: Simon Peter said to Him, "Lord, where are You going?" Jesus answered him, "Where I am going you cannot follow Me now, but you will follow later."
verses.13:37: Peter said to Him, "Lord, why can I not follow You right now? I will lay down my life for You."
verses.13:38: Jesus answered, "Will you lay down your life for Me? Truly, truly, I tell you, a rooster will not crow until you have denied Me three times."
verses.14:1: "Do not let your heart be troubled. Believe in God, and believe in Me as well.
verses.14:2: In My Father's house there are many dwelling places; if it were not so, I would have told you, because I am going to prepare a place for you.
verses.14:3: And if I go and prepare a place for you, I am coming again and will take you to Myself, so that where I am, you also may be.
verses.14:4: And where I am going, you know the way."
verses.14:5: Thomas said to Him, "Lord, we do not know where You are going; how can we know the way?"
verses.14:6: Jesus told him, "I am the way and the truth and the life; no one comes to the Father except through Me.
verses.14:7: If you had known Me, you would have known My Father as well. From now on you know Him and have seen Him."
verses.14:8: Philip said to Him, "Lord, show us the Father, and it is enough for us."
verses.14:9: Jesus said to him, "Have I been with you so long a time, and yet you have not known Me, Philip? The one who has seen Me has seen the Father. How do you say, 'Show us the Father'?
verses.14:10: Do you not believe that I am in the Father and the Father is in Me? The words that I speak to you I do not speak from Myself, but the Father remaining in Me does His works.
verses.14:11: Believe Me that I am in the Father and the Father is in Me; otherwise, believe because of the works themselves.
verses.14:12: Truly, truly, I tell you, the one who believes in Me, he also will do the works that I do; and he will do greater things than these, because I am going to the Father.
verses.14:13: And whatever you ask in My name, this I will do, so that the Father may be glorified in the Son.
verses.14:14: If you ask Me anything in My name, I will do it.
verses.14:15: If you love Me, you will keep My commandments.
verses.14:16: And I will ask the Father, and He will give you another Advocate, so that He may be with you forever,
verses.14:17: the Spirit of truth, whom the world cannot receive, because it neither sees Him nor knows Him. You know Him, because He remains with you and will be in you.
verses.14:18: I will not leave you orphans; I am coming to you.
verses.14:19: In a little while the world will see Me no longer, yet you will see Me; because I live, you also will live.
verses.14:20: On that day you will know that I am in My Father, and you in Me, and I in you.
verses.14:21: The one who has My commandments and keeps them, that is the one who loves Me; and the one who loves Me will be loved by My Father, and I will love him and will reveal Myself to him."
verses.14:22: Judas (not Iscariot) said to Him, "Lord, what has happened that You are about to reveal Yourself to us and not to the world?"
verses.14:23: Jesus answered and said to him, "If anyone loves Me, he will keep My word; and My Father will love him, and We will come to him and make Our dwelling with him.
verses.14:24: The one who does not love Me does not keep My words; and the word that you hear is not Mine, but that of the Father who sent Me.
verses.14:25: These things I have spoken to you while remaining with you.
verses.14:26: But the Advocate, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in My name—He will teach you all things and remind you of all things that I said to you.
