verses.14:27: Peace I leave with you; My own peace I give to you. Not as the world gives do I give to you. Do not let your heart be troubled, nor let it be afraid.
verses.14:28: You heard that I said to you, 'I am going away, and I am coming to you.' If you loved Me, you would have rejoiced that I am going to the Father, because the Father is greater than I.
verses.14:29: And now I have told you before it happens, so that when it happens you may believe.
verses.14:30: I will no longer speak much with you, for the ruler of the world is coming, and he has nothing in Me—
verses.14:31: but so that the world may know that I love the Father, just as the Father commanded Me, so I do. Get up, let us go from here."
verses.15:1: "I am the true vine, and My Father is the vinegrower.
verses.15:2: Every branch in Me that does not bear fruit He takes away, and every branch that bears fruit He prunes, so that it may bear more fruit.
verses.15:3: Already you are clean because of the word that I have spoken to you.
verses.15:4: Remain in Me, and I in you. Just as the branch cannot bear fruit on its own unless it remains in the vine, so neither can you unless you remain in Me.
verses.15:5: I am the vine, you are the branches. The one who remains in Me and I in him, he bears much fruit, because apart from Me you can do nothing.
verses.15:6: If anyone does not remain in Me, he is thrown outside like a branch and withers; and they gather them and cast them into the fire, and they burn.
verses.15:7: If you remain in Me and My words remain in you, ask for whatever you wish, and it will be done for you.
verses.15:8: By this My Father is glorified, that you bear much fruit and become My disciples.
verses.15:9: Just as the Father loved Me, I also loved you; remain in My love.
verses.15:10: If you keep My commandments, you will remain in My love, just as I have kept the Father's commandments and remain in His love.
verses.15:11: These things I have spoken to you so that My joy may be in you, and that your joy may be made full.
verses.15:12: This is My commandment, that you love one another just as I loved you.
verses.15:13: No one has greater love than this, that someone lay down his life on behalf of his friends.
verses.15:14: You are My friends if you do the things that I command you.
verses.15:15: No longer do I call you slaves, because a slave does not know what his master is doing; instead, I have called you friends, because all the things that I heard from My Father I made known to you.
verses.15:16: You did not choose Me, rather I chose you and appointed you so that you would go and bear fruit and that your fruit would remain, so that whatever you ask the Father in My name, He may give to you.
verses.15:17: These things I command you, so that you love one another.
verses.15:18: If the world hates you, know that it has hated Me before you.
verses.15:19: If you were of the world, the world would love its own; yet because you are not of the world, rather I chose you out of the world, for this reason the world hates you.
verses.15:20: Remember the word that I spoke to you: 'A slave is not greater than his master.' If they persecuted Me, they will persecute you as well; if they kept My word, they will keep yours as well.
verses.15:21: Yet all these things they will do to you on account of My name, because they do not know the One who sent Me.
verses.15:22: If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not have sin; now, however, they have no excuse concerning their sin.
verses.15:23: The one who hates Me hates My Father also.
verses.15:24: If I had not done among them the works that no one else did, they would not have sin; now, however, they have both seen and hated both Me and My Father.
verses.15:25: Yet this is so that the word written in their Law may be fulfilled: 'They hated Me without cause.'
verses.15:26: When the Advocate comes, whom I will send to you from the Father, the Spirit of truth who proceeds from the Father, He will testify concerning Me;
verses.15:27: and you also testify, because you have been with Me from the beginning."
verses.16:1: "These things I have spoken to you so that you may not be made to stumble.
verses.16:2: They will put you out of the synagogue; indeed, an hour is coming when everyone who kills you will think he is offering sacred service to God.
verses.16:3: And these things they will do because they have not known the Father nor Me.
verses.16:4: Yet these things I have spoken to you so that when their hour comes, you may remember them, that I told you. These things, however, I did not tell you from the beginning, because I was with you.
verses.16:5: Now, however, I am going to the One who sent Me, and none of you asks Me, 'Where are You going?'
verses.16:6: Instead, because I have spoken these things to you, sorrow has filled your heart.
verses.16:7: Yet I tell you the truth: it is to your advantage that I go away. For if I do not go away, the Advocate will not come to you; if, however, I depart, I will send Him to you.
verses.16:8: And when He comes, He will convict the world concerning sin, and concerning righteousness, and concerning judgment:
verses.16:9: concerning sin, because they do not believe in Me;
verses.16:10: concerning righteousness, because I am going to the Father and you see Me no longer;
verses.16:11: and concerning judgment, because the ruler of this world has been judged.
verses.16:12: I still have many things to say to you, yet you cannot bear them now.
verses.16:13: When He comes, however, the Spirit of truth, He will guide you into all the truth; for He will not speak on His own, rather whatever He will hear He will speak, and He will declare to you the things that are coming.
verses.16:14: He will glorify Me, because He will take from what is Mine and declare it to you.
verses.16:15: Everything that the Father has is Mine; for this reason I said that He takes from what is Mine and will declare it to you.
verses.16:16: A little while, and you no longer see Me; and again a little while, and you will see Me."
verses.16:17: So some of His disciples said to one another, "What is this that He is telling us, 'A little while, and you do not see Me; and again a little while, and you will see Me'; and, 'Because I am going to the Father'?"
verses.16:18: So they were saying, "What is this 'little while' that He says? We do not know what He is speaking about."
verses.16:19: Jesus knew that they wanted to question Him, and He said to them, "Are you inquiring with one another about this, that I said, 'A little while, and you do not see Me; and again a little while, and you will see Me'?
verses.16:20: Truly, truly, I say to you that you will weep and lament, while the world will rejoice; you will be sorrowful, yet your sorrow will turn into joy.
verses.16:21: When a woman is giving birth she has sorrow, because her hour has come; when, however, she has delivered the child, she no longer remembers the distress, because of the joy that a human being has been born into the world.
verses.16:22: So you also have sorrow now; yet I will see you again, and your heart will rejoice, and no one takes your joy away from you.
verses.16:23: And on that day you will not question Me about anything. Truly, truly, I say to you, whatever you ask the Father, He will give to you in My name.
verses.16:24: Until now you have asked for nothing in My name; ask and you will receive, so that your joy may be made full.
verses.16:25: These things I have spoken to you in figures of speech; an hour is coming when I will no longer speak to you in figures of speech, rather I will tell you plainly about the Father.
verses.16:26: On that day you will ask in My name, and I am not saying to you that I will ask the Father on your behalf;
verses.16:27: for the Father Himself loves you, because you have loved Me and have believed that I came forth from God.
verses.16:28: I came forth from the Father and have come into the world; again, I am leaving the world and going to the Father."
verses.16:29: His disciples say, "Look, now You are speaking plainly and are saying no figure of speech.
verses.16:30: Now we know that You know all things and have no need for anyone to question You; by this we believe that You came forth from God."
verses.16:31: Jesus answered them, "Do you now believe?
verses.16:32: Look, an hour is coming, and has come, when you will be scattered, each one to his own home, and will leave Me alone; and yet I am not alone, because the Father is with Me.
verses.16:33: These things I have spoken to you so that in Me you may have peace. In the world you have distress, yet take courage: I have conquered the world."
verses.17:1: Jesus spoke these things, and lifting up His eyes to heaven, He said, "Father, the hour has come; glorify Your Son, so that the Son may glorify You,
verses.17:2: just as You gave Him authority over all flesh, so that for all that You have given Him, He may give them eternal life.
verses.17:3: Now this is eternal life: that they may know You, the only true God, and the One whom You sent, Jesus Christ.
verses.17:4: I glorified You on the earth, having completed the work that You have given Me to do;
verses.17:5: and now You, Father, glorify Me in Your own presence with the glory that I had with You before the world existed.
verses.17:6: I revealed Your name to the people whom You gave Me out of the world. They were Yours, and to Me You gave them, and they have kept Your word.
verses.17:7: Now they have come to know that all the things You have given Me are from You;
verses.17:8: because the words that You gave Me I have given to them, and they received them and truly knew that I came out from You, and they believed that You sent Me.
verses.17:9: I am asking on their behalf; I am not asking on behalf of the world, but on behalf of those whom You have given Me, because they are Yours,
verses.17:10: and all things that are Mine are Yours, and what is Yours is Mine, and I have been glorified in them.
verses.17:11: And I am no longer in the world, and they are in the world, and I am coming to You. Holy Father, keep them in Your name that You have given Me, so that they may be one, just as We are.
verses.17:12: While I was with them, I was keeping them in Your name that You have given Me, and I guarded them, and not one of them perished except the son of destruction, so that the Scripture might be fulfilled.
verses.17:13: But now I am coming to You, and I speak these things in the world so that they may have My joy made full in themselves.
verses.17:14: I have given Your word to them, and the world hated them, because they are not from the world, just as I am not from the world.
verses.17:15: I am not asking that You take them out of the world, but that You keep them from the evil one.
verses.17:16: They are not from the world, just as I am not from the world.
verses.17:17: Consecrate them in the truth; Your word is truth.
verses.17:18: Just as You sent Me into the world, I also sent them into the world;
verses.17:19: and on their behalf I consecrate Myself, so that they also may be consecrated in truth.
verses.17:20: Now I am not asking on behalf of these alone, but also on behalf of those who believe in Me through their word,
verses.17:21: so that all of them may be one, just as You, Father, are in Me and I in You, so that they also may be in Us, so that the world may believe that You sent Me.
verses.17:22: And the glory that You have given Me, I have given to them, so that they may be one, just as We are one,
verses.17:23: I in them and You in Me, so that they may be brought to completion into one, so that the world may know that You sent Me and loved them just as You loved Me.
verses.17:24: Father, what You have given Me—I desire that where I am, they also may be with Me, so that they may see My glory that You have given Me, because You loved Me before the foundation of the world.
verses.17:25: Righteous Father, although the world did not know You, I knew You, and these knew that You sent Me,
verses.17:26: and I made Your name known to them and will make it known, so that the love with which You loved Me may be in them, and I in them."
verses.18:1: Having said these things, Jesus went out with His disciples across the winter stream of the Kidron, where there was a garden, into which He Himself and His disciples entered.
verses.18:2: Now Judas, the one handing Him over, also knew the place, because Jesus had often gathered there with His disciples.
verses.18:3: So Judas, having taken the cohort and attendants from the chief priests and from the Pharisees, came there with lanterns and torches and weapons.
verses.18:4: Then Jesus, knowing all the things that were coming upon Him, went out and said to them, "Whom are you seeking?"
verses.18:5: They answered Him, "Jesus the Nazarene." He said to them, "I am." Now Judas, the one handing Him over, was also standing with them.
verses.18:6: So when He said to them, "I am," they drew back and fell to the ground.
verses.18:7: Therefore He asked them again, "Whom are you seeking?" And they said, "Jesus the Nazarene."
verses.18:8: Jesus answered, "I told you that I am; so if you are seeking Me, let these go,"
verses.18:9: so that the word that He spoke might be fulfilled: "Of those whom You have given Me, I did not lose a single one."
verses.18:10: Then Simon Peter, having a sword, drew it and struck the slave of the high priest and cut off his right ear. Now the slave's name was Malchus.
verses.18:11: So Jesus said to Peter, "Put the sword into the sheath; the cup that the Father has given Me, shall I not drink it?"
verses.18:12: Then the cohort and the commander and the attendants of the Jews seized Jesus and bound Him,
verses.18:13: and led Him to Annas first; for he was the father-in-law of Caiaphas, who was high priest that year.
verses.18:14: Now Caiaphas was the one who had advised the Jews that it was beneficial for one man to die on behalf of the people.
verses.18:15: Now Simon Peter was following Jesus, and so was another disciple. And that disciple was known to the high priest, and entered with Jesus into the courtyard of the high priest,
verses.18:16: but Peter was standing outside at the door. So the other disciple, who was known to the high priest, went out and spoke to the doorkeeper and brought Peter in.
verses.18:17: Then the servant girl who was the doorkeeper said to Peter, "You are not also one of this man's disciples, are you?" He said, "I am not."
verses.18:18: Now the slaves and the attendants were standing there, having made a charcoal fire because it was cold, and they were warming themselves; and Peter was also with them, standing and warming himself.
verses.18:19: So the high priest questioned Jesus about His disciples and about His teaching.
verses.18:20: Jesus answered him, "I have spoken openly to the world; I always taught in synagogue and in the temple, where all the Jews assemble, and in secret I spoke nothing.
verses.18:21: Why do you question Me? Question those who have heard what I spoke to them; look, these people know what I said."
verses.18:22: Now when He had said these things, one of the attendants standing nearby gave Jesus a slap, saying, "Do You answer the high priest like this?"
verses.18:23: Jesus answered him, "If I spoke wrongly, testify about the wrong; but if rightly, why do you strike Me?"
verses.18:24: So Annas sent Him bound to Caiaphas the high priest.
verses.18:25: Now Simon Peter was standing and warming himself. So they said to him, "You are not also one of His disciples, are you?" He denied it and said, "I am not."
verses.18:26: One of the slaves of the high priest, being a relative of the one whose ear Peter cut off, said, "Did I not see you in the garden with Him?"
verses.18:27: So Peter denied it again, and immediately a rooster crowed.
verses.18:28: Then they led Jesus from Caiaphas into the Praetorium, and it was early morning. And they themselves did not enter into the Praetorium, so that they might not be defiled, but might eat the Passover.
verses.18:29: Therefore Pilate went outside to them and said, "What accusation do you bring against this man?"
verses.18:30: They answered and said to him, "If this man were not doing evil, we would not have handed Him over to you."
verses.18:31: So Pilate said to them, "Take Him yourselves, and judge Him according to your law." The Jews said to him, "It is not permitted for us to put anyone to death,"
verses.18:32: so that the word of Jesus might be fulfilled that He spoke, indicating by what kind of death He was about to die.
verses.18:33: Therefore Pilate entered into the Praetorium again and summoned Jesus and said to Him, "Are You the King of the Jews?"
verses.18:34: Jesus answered, "Are you saying this on your own, or did others tell you about Me?"
verses.18:35: Pilate answered, "I am not a Jew, am I? Your own nation and the chief priests handed You over to me; what did You do?"
verses.18:36: Jesus answered, "My kingdom is not from this world. If My kingdom were from this world, My attendants would be fighting so that I would not be handed over to the Jews; but as it is, My kingdom is not from here."
verses.18:37: Therefore Pilate said to Him, "So then, You are a king?" Jesus answered, "You say that I am a king. For this I have been born, and for this I have come into the world, to testify to the truth. Everyone who is of the truth hears My voice."
verses.18:38: Pilate said to Him, "What is truth?" And having said this, he went out again to the Jews and said to them, "I find no grounds for a charge in Him;
verses.18:39: but you have a custom that I release one person to you at the Passover. Do you wish, then, that I release to you the King of the Jews?"
verses.18:40: Then they cried out again, saying, "Not this man, but Barabbas!" Now Barabbas was a bandit.
verses.19:1: So then Pilate took Jesus and flogged Him.
verses.19:2: And the soldiers twisted together a crown of thorns and set it on His head, and put a purple robe around Him.
verses.19:3: And they kept coming up to Him and saying, "Hail, King of the Jews!" and they kept slapping Him.
verses.19:4: And Pilate went outside again and said to them, "Look, I am bringing Him out to you so that you may know that I find no grounds at all for a charge in Him."
verses.19:5: So Jesus came outside, wearing the crown of thorns and the purple robe. And he said to them, "Here is the man."
verses.19:6: Therefore, when the chief priests and the officers saw Him, they shouted, saying, "Crucify! Crucify!" Pilate said to them, "Take Him yourselves and crucify Him, for I myself find no grounds for a charge in Him."
verses.19:7: The Jews answered him, "We have a law, and according to the law He must die, because He made Himself the Son of God."
verses.19:8: Therefore, when Pilate heard this statement, he became even more afraid.
verses.19:9: And he entered the Praetorium again and said to Jesus, "Where are You from?" But Jesus did not give him an answer.
verses.19:10: So Pilate said to Him, "Are You not speaking to me? Do You not know that I have authority to release You, and I have authority to crucify You?"
verses.19:11: Jesus answered him, "You would have no authority at all against Me unless it had been given to you from above. For this reason, the one who handed Me over to you has greater sin."
verses.19:12: From then on Pilate kept seeking to release Him, but the Jews shouted, saying, "If you release this man, you are no friend of Caesar. Everyone who makes himself a king speaks against Caesar."
verses.19:13: Therefore, when Pilate heard these words, he brought Jesus outside and sat down on the judgment seat at a place called the Stone Pavement, and in Hebrew, Gabbatha.
verses.19:14: Now it was the day of Preparation for the Passover; it was about the sixth hour. And he said to the Jews, "Here is your King!"
verses.19:15: But they shouted, "Take Him away! Take Him away! Crucify Him!" Pilate said to them, "Should I crucify your King?" The chief priests answered, "We have no king except Caesar."
verses.19:16: So then he handed Him over to them so that He would be crucified. And they took Jesus.
verses.19:17: And carrying the cross for Himself, He went out to what is called the Place of a Skull, which in Hebrew is called Golgotha.
verses.19:18: There they crucified Him, and with Him two others, one on this side and one on that side, with Jesus in the middle.
verses.19:19: Now Pilate also wrote an inscription and placed it on the cross. And what was written was, "Jesus the Nazarene, the King of the Jews."
verses.19:20: Therefore many of the Jews read this inscription, because the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city; and it was written in Hebrew, in Latin, and in Greek.
verses.19:21: So the chief priests of the Jews were saying to Pilate, "Do not write, 'The King of the Jews,' but that He said, 'I am King of the Jews.'"
verses.19:22: Pilate answered, "What I have written, I have written."
verses.19:23: Therefore, when the soldiers had crucified Jesus, they took His garments and made four parts, a part for each soldier, and the tunic as well. Now the tunic was seamless, woven from the top all the way through.
verses.19:24: So they said to one another, "Let us not tear it, but let us cast lots for it as to whose it will be," so that the Scripture would be fulfilled that says, "They divided My garments among themselves, and for My clothing they cast lots." So the soldiers did these things.
verses.19:25: Now standing beside the cross of Jesus were His mother and His mother's sister, Mary the wife of Clopas, and Mary Magdalene.
verses.19:26: Therefore, when Jesus saw His mother and the disciple whom He loved standing nearby, He said to His mother, "Woman, here is your son."
verses.19:27: Then He said to the disciple, "Here is your mother." And from that hour the disciple took her into his own home.
verses.19:28: After this, Jesus, knowing that all things were already finished, so that the Scripture might be fulfilled, said, "I am thirsty."
verses.19:29: A jar full of sour wine was sitting there, so they put a sponge full of the sour wine on a hyssop branch and brought it to His mouth.
verses.19:30: So when Jesus had taken the sour wine, He said, "It is finished." And bowing His head, He yielded up His spirit.
verses.19:31: Then the Jews, because it was the day of Preparation, so that the bodies would not remain on the cross during the Sabbath (for the day of that Sabbath was a great day), asked Pilate that their legs be broken and that they be taken away.
verses.19:32: So the soldiers came and broke the legs of the first man, and of the other who was crucified with Him.
verses.19:33: But upon coming to Jesus, when they saw that He was already dead, they did not break His legs.
verses.19:34: Instead, one of the soldiers pierced His side with a spear, and immediately blood and water came out.
verses.19:35: And the one who has seen this has testified, and his testimony is true; and he knows that he speaks the truth, so that you also may believe.
verses.19:36: For these things took place so that the Scripture might be fulfilled, "No bone of His will be broken."
verses.19:37: And again another Scripture says, "They will look upon Him whom they pierced."
verses.19:38: Now after these things, Joseph from Arimathea, who was a disciple of Jesus, though in secret because of fear of the Jews, asked Pilate that he might take away the body of Jesus; and Pilate permitted it. So he came and took away His body.
verses.19:39: And Nicodemus also came, the one who had first come to Him by night, bringing a mixture of myrrh and aloes, about a hundred pounds.
verses.19:40: So they took the body of Jesus and bound it in linen cloths with the spices, just as is the custom of the Jews in preparing for burial.
verses.19:41: Now in the place where He was crucified there was a garden, and in the garden a new tomb in which no one had yet been laid.
verses.19:42: So there, because of the Jews' day of Preparation, since the tomb was nearby, they laid Jesus.
verses.20:1: Now on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene came early, while it was still dark, to the tomb, and she saw the stone taken away from the tomb.
verses.20:2: Therefore she ran and came to Simon Peter and to the other disciple whom Jesus loved, and she said to them, "They have taken the Lord from the tomb, and we do not know where they have placed Him."
verses.20:3: So Peter and the other disciple went out, and they were going to the tomb.
verses.20:4: Now the two were running together, and the other disciple ran ahead faster than Peter and came to the tomb first.
verses.20:5: And bending down, he saw the linen cloths lying there; however, he did not go in.
verses.20:6: Then Simon Peter also came, following him, and entered the tomb, and he observed the linen cloths lying there,
verses.20:7: and the face cloth that had been on His head, not lying with the linen cloths, but rolled up separately in one place.
verses.20:8: Then the other disciple, who had come to the tomb first, also went in, and he saw and believed.
verses.20:9: For they had not yet understood the Scripture, that He must rise from the dead.
verses.20:10: So the disciples departed again to their own homes.
verses.20:11: But Mary stood weeping outside at the tomb; and as she was weeping, she stooped down to look into the tomb,
verses.20:12: and she observed two angels in white sitting there, one at the head and one at the feet, where the body of Jesus had been lying.
verses.20:13: And they said to her, "Woman, why are you weeping?" She said to them, "They have taken my Lord, and I do not know where they have placed Him."
verses.20:14: Having said these things, she turned around and observed Jesus standing there, and she did not know that it was Jesus.
verses.20:15: Jesus said to her, "Woman, why are you weeping? Whom are you looking for?" Supposing that He was the gardener, she said to Him, "Sir, if you have carried Him away, tell me where you have placed Him, and I will take Him away."
verses.20:16: Jesus said to her, "Mary!" Turning around, she said to Him in Hebrew, "Rabboni!" (which means, "Teacher").
verses.20:17: Jesus said to her, "Do not hold on to Me, for I have not yet ascended to the Father; but go to My brothers and tell them, 'I am ascending to My Father and your Father, and My God and your God.'"
verses.20:18: Mary Magdalene came announcing to the disciples, "I have seen the Lord," and that He had said these things to her.
verses.20:19: Now when it was evening on that day, the first day of the week, and while the doors were shut where the disciples were for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood in their midst and said to them, "Peace be with you."
verses.20:20: Having said this, He showed them His hands and His side. The disciples therefore rejoiced when they saw the Lord.
verses.20:21: So Jesus said to them again, "Peace be with you; just as the Father has sent Me, I also am sending you."
verses.20:22: And when He had said this, He breathed on them and said to them, "Receive the Holy Spirit.
verses.20:23: If you forgive the sins of any, they have been forgiven them; if you retain the sins of any, they have been retained."
verses.20:24: Now Thomas, one of the twelve, who is called Didymus, was not with them when Jesus came.
verses.20:25: So the other disciples were saying to him, "We have seen the Lord!" But he said to them, "Unless I see the mark of the nails in His hands, and put my finger into the mark of the nails, and put my hand into His side, I will never believe."
verses.20:26: And after eight days His disciples were inside again, and Thomas was with them. Jesus came while the doors were shut, and stood in their midst, and said, "Peace be with you."
verses.20:27: Then He said to Thomas, "Bring your finger here and see My hands, and bring your hand and put it into My side; and do not become unbelieving, but believing."
verses.20:28: Thomas answered and said to Him, "My Lord and my God!"
verses.20:29: Jesus said to him, "Because you have seen Me, have you believed? Blessed are those who did not see, and believed."
verses.20:30: Therefore Jesus also performed many other signs in the presence of His disciples, which are not written in this book;
verses.20:31: but these things are written so that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that by believing you may have life in His name.
verses.21:1: After these things Jesus revealed Himself again to the disciples by the Sea of Tiberias; and He revealed Himself in this way.
verses.21:2: Simon Peter, Thomas who is called Didymus, Nathanael from Cana of Galilee, the sons of Zebedee, and two others of His disciples were together.
verses.21:3: Simon Peter said to them, "I am going fishing." They said to him, "We are also coming with you." They went out and got into the boat, and during that night they caught nothing.
verses.21:4: Now when morning had already come, Jesus stood on the shore; yet the disciples did not know that it was Jesus.
verses.21:5: Jesus therefore said to them, "Children, you have no fish, do you?" They replied to Him, "No."
verses.21:6: And He said to them, "Cast the net on the right side of the boat, and you will find some." So they cast it, and they were no longer able to haul it in because of the multitude of fish.
verses.21:7: Therefore that disciple whom Jesus loved said to Peter, "It is the Lord!" So when Simon Peter heard that it was the Lord, he tied his outer garment around himself, for he was naked, and threw himself into the sea.
verses.21:8: But the other disciples came in the little boat, for they were not far from the land, only about two hundred cubits away, dragging the net of fish.
verses.21:9: So when they stepped out onto the land, they saw a charcoal fire in place, and fish lying on it, and bread.
verses.21:10: Jesus said to them, "Bring some of the fish that you have just caught."
verses.21:11: So Simon Peter went aboard and hauled the net onto the land, full of large fish, one hundred fifty-three; and although there were so many, the net was not torn.
verses.21:12: Jesus said to them, "Come, have breakfast." Now none of the disciples dared to question Him, "Who are You?" knowing that it was the Lord.
verses.21:13: Jesus came and took the bread and gave it to them, and the fish likewise.
verses.21:14: This was now the third time Jesus was revealed to the disciples after being raised from the dead.
verses.21:15: So when they had finished breakfast, Jesus said to Simon Peter, "Simon, son of John, do you love Me more than these?" He said to Him, "Yes, Lord; You know that I love You." He said to him, "Feed My lambs."
verses.21:16: He said to him again a second time, "Simon, son of John, do you love Me?" He said to Him, "Yes, Lord; You know that I love You." He said to him, "Shepherd My sheep."
verses.21:17: He said to him the third time, "Simon, son of John, do you love Me?" Peter was grieved because He said to him the third time, "Do you love Me?" And he said to Him, "Lord, You know all things; You know that I love You." Jesus said to him, "Feed My sheep.
verses.21:18: Truly, truly, I say to you, when you were younger, you used to dress yourself and walk wherever you wanted; but when you grow old, you will stretch out your hands, and another will dress you and carry you where you do not want to go."
verses.21:19: Now He said this, signifying by what kind of death he would glorify God. And when He had said this, He said to him, "Follow Me."
verses.21:20: Turning around, Peter saw the disciple whom Jesus loved following them, the one who also had leaned back on His chest at the supper and had said, "Lord, who is the one betraying You?"
verses.21:21: So seeing him, Peter said to Jesus, "Lord, and what about this man?"
verses.21:22: Jesus said to him, "If I want him to remain until I come, what is that to you? You follow Me!"
verses.21:23: Therefore this saying went out among the brothers that that disciple would not die. Yet Jesus did not say to him that he would not die, but, "If I want him to remain until I come, what is that to you?"
verses.21:24: This is the disciple who testifies about these things and who wrote these things, and we know that his testimony is true.
verses.21:25: Now there are also many other things that Jesus did, which, if they were written one by one, I suppose that not even the world itself could contain the books that would be written.

notes.1:1: In the final clause (θεὸς ἦν ὁ λόγος), ὁ λόγος ("the Word") has the article and is the subject, while θεός ("God") is placed first without an article as a qualitative predicate. Rendered "the Word was God" to preserve both the subject-predicate order in English and the affirmation of the Word's full deity.
notes.1:3: The Saints Greek Critical Text places a period after οὐδὲ ἕν ("not even one thing"), joining ὃ γέγονεν ("what has come into being") to the start of 1:4 rather than ending 1:3 with "that was made." The translation follows the Greek punctuation.
notes.1:5: κατέλαβεν carries a deliberate double resonance in John: "overtake/overcome" (hostile darkness failing to extinguish the light) and "comprehend/grasp." "Overtake" keeps the primary spatial and conflict sense of the verb.
notes.1:9: The participle ἐρχόμενον ("coming") is grammatically ambiguous: it can modify "the true light" (rendered here) or "every person" ("illuminates every person coming into the world").
notes.1:11: The Greek shifts from neuter plural τὰ ἴδια ("His own things/domain") to masculine plural οἱ ἴδιοι ("His own people"). Both are reflected distinctly.
notes.1:13: ἐξ αἱμάτων uses the plural "bloods" (rendered "bloodlines"), referring to physical descent, and ἀνδρός specifically means a male/husband rather than a generic human being.
notes.1:14: ἐσκήνωσεν literally means "pitched a tent" or "tabernacled," recalling God's dwelling among Israel in the tabernacle. μονογενοῦς means "only-begotten" or "unique, one of a kind."
notes.1:16: χάριν ἀντὶ χάριτος literally means "grace in place of grace" (one gift of grace succeeding or replacing another, often understood as grace upon grace or the grace of Christ superseding the grace of the law).
notes.1:18: The Saints Greek Critical Text reads μονογενὴς θεός ("only-begotten God" or "the unique God"), rather than the later variant "only-begotten Son." εἰς τὸν κόλπον literally means "into the bosom/embrace," an idiom for closest intimacy, rendered "at the Father's side." ἐξηγήσατο ("explained, narrated, made known") has no explicit object in Greek; "Him" is supplied for English clarity.
notes.1:21: John frequently uses the historical present (λέγει, "he says"; βλέπει, "he sees"; εὑρίσκει, "he finds") throughout 1:21–51. It is retained here to preserve the vividness of the Greek narrative.
notes.1:51: Ἀμὴν ἀμήν (literally "Amen, amen") is rendered "Truly, truly." The "you" in "I tell you" and "you will see" is plural (ὑμῖν, ὄψεσθε), addressing all the disciples present.
notes.2:4: The Greek phrase literally asks "What to Me and to you?", a Semitic idiom distancing the speaker from another's concern or request. Addressing Mary as "woman" (gynai) was polite and respectful in ancient Greek, not disrespectful.
notes.2:6: A Greek metretes ("measure") was a liquid unit of roughly 9 to 10 gallons (about 35 to 40 liters), meaning each stone jar held approximately 20 to 30 gallons.
notes.2:19: John uses naos ("sanctuary," referring to the inner temple building) here and in vv. 20-21, distinguishing it from hieron ("temple," the entire temple precinct) in vv. 14-15.
notes.2:24: John plays on the verb pisteuo: while many "believed" in Jesus' name (v. 23), Jesus was not "entrusting" Himself to them (v. 24).
notes.3:3: The Greek adverb anothen carries a deliberate double meaning: both "from above" (as in 3:31) and "again" (the sense Nicodemus hears in v. 4).
notes.3:8: The verse turns on a wordplay with Greek pneuma, which means both "wind" and "Spirit," paired with the related verb pnei ("blows").
notes.3:16: Greek houtos can denote manner ("in this way") or degree ("so"), and monogenes ("only-begotten," matching 1:14, 18) denotes a unique, one-of-a-kind son. Because ancient Greek lacked quotation marks, scholars debate whether Jesus' speech ends at v. 15 or continues through v. 21.
notes.3:31: Because ancient Greek manuscripts have no quotation marks, interpreters debate whether vv. 31-36 continue the speech of John the Baptist or shift to the narrator's reflection.
notes.4:9: Greek συγχρῶνται literally means "use together with," which may refer specifically to sharing drinking vessels in addition to broader social dealings between Jews and Samaritans.
notes.4:26: Greek Ἐγώ εἰμι is literally "I am," serving both as a predicate identification ("I am He") and as an echo of the divine self-designation in the Greek Old Testament (cf. Exod 3:14; Isa 43:10).
notes.4:35: In the Greek text, ἤδη ("Already") appears after the punctuation break at the end of v. 35 to open the sentence completed in v. 36, though some punctuation traditions attach it to v. 35 ("already white for harvest").
notes.4:48: Both verbs ("see" and "believe") are second-person plural in Greek, showing that Jesus addresses not only the royal official individually but the wider Galilean audience as well.
notes.5:2: The Greek reads literally 'by the sheep' (with 'Gate' implied, cf. Neh 3:1). Early manuscripts vary on the pool's name among Bethzatha, Bethesda, and Bethsaida, and 'in Hebrew' refers here to the Semitic vernacular (Aramaic) spoken in Judea.
notes.5:3: The earliest and most reliable Greek manuscripts omit 'waiting for the moving of the water' at the end of v. 3 and all of v. 4 (about an angel stirring the water), so v. 4 is absent from the critical text.
notes.5:27: The Greek phrase 'Son of Man' is uniquely without the definite article here, recalling both the heavenly judge of Daniel 7:13-14 and Jesus' genuine humanity.
notes.5:39: The Greek verb 'eraunate' can be construed as either an indicative ('You search') or an imperative ('Search!'); the indicative fits the flow of the argument best in contrast with v. 40.
notes.6:19: A stadion was a Greek unit of length of about 600 feet (185 meters), so twenty-five to thirty stadia was roughly 3 to 3.5 miles (4.5 to 5.5 kilometers).
notes.6:20: Greek ego eimi, literally 'I am,' functions idiomatically as self-identification ('It is I') while also echoing the divine self-designation of Exodus 3:14 and Isaiah.
notes.6:33: The masculine participle ho katabainon agrees grammatically with masculine artos ('bread') and may be rendered either 'that which descends' or 'He who descends,' anticipating Jesus' self-identification in verse 35.
notes.6:34: Greek Kyrie can mean either 'Lord' or respectful 'Sir,' reflecting the crowd's deference even as they still misunderstand the bread Jesus offers.
notes.6:54: Greek trogo (vv. 54, 56-58) literally denotes chewing or eating and functions as the present-tense counterpart to aorist phago ('eat') in vv. 49-53, emphasizing real, ongoing participation.
notes.6:62: The Greek is an elliptical conditional question ('What if, then...'), leaving the implied result unstated for the listeners to weigh.
notes.7:8: The Greek text reads oupo ("not yet"); several early manuscripts read ouk ("not").
notes.7:22: The phrase dia touto ("Because of this") begins v. 22 here, though some punctuation traditions attach it to the end of v. 21 ("and you all marvel because of it").
notes.7:38: Greek koilia literally means "belly" or "interior" and denotes the inner being; an alternative punctuation joins "the one who believes in Me" to "and drink" in v. 37, making "his" refer to Christ rather than the believer.
notes.7:39: Literally "for the Spirit was not yet," expressing that the Spirit had not yet been given prior to Jesus's glorification; some later manuscripts add dedomenon ("given").
notes.7:53: Double brackets ⟦ ⟧ are preserved around 7:53–8:11 exactly as in the Saints Greek Critical Text, marking the pericope of the adulterous woman, which is absent from the earliest Greek manuscripts.
notes.8:6: The Saints Greek Critical Text includes the participial phrase μὴ προσποιούμενος ("not taking notice / acting as though He did not notice"), which is translated here.
notes.8:7: τὸν λίθον carries the definite article ("the stone"), referring to the first stone in a stoning execution, and πρῶτον is adverbial ("first").
notes.8:9: The Saints Greek Critical Text includes καὶ ὑπὸ τῆς συνειδήσεως ἐλεγχόμενοι ("and being convicted by their conscience"), which appears in the Byzantine textual tradition.
notes.8:11: While 8:10 uses κατέκρινεν ("condemn"), the Saints Greek Critical Text here reads the simple verb κρίνω ("judge"), preserved distinctly as "judge."
notes.8:24: The Greek phrase "egō eimi" ("I am") lacks a predicate here (as also in 8:28 and 8:58), echoing God's self-revelation in Exodus 3:14 and Isaiah 43:10.
notes.8:25: The Greek construction "Tēn archēn ho ti kai lalō hymin;" is famously difficult; punctuated as a question in the critical text it means "Why am I even speaking to you at all?" though it is alternatively read as a statement, "Just what I have been telling you from the beginning."
notes.8:38: The critical text reads "from the father" without a possessive pronoun, leaving the identity of their father ambiguous until Jesus explicitly names the devil in 8:44.
notes.8:44: The final clause "the father of it" ("ho patēr autou") most naturally refers back to "a lie" (falsehood), though some take it to mean "the father of the liar."
notes.8:58: Jesus contrasts the aorist infinitive "genesthai" ("came into being") for Abraham with the timeless present "egō eimi" ("I am"), asserting divine preexistence in echo of Exodus 3:14.
notes.9:4: The earliest Greek manuscripts read "We must... the One who sent Me" (translated here), whereas later manuscripts harmonize the opening pronoun to "I must."
notes.9:24: "Give glory to God" is an Old Testament formula of solemn adjuration calling on someone to speak the truth before God (cf. Joshua 7:19).
notes.9:35: The earliest Greek manuscripts read "the Son of Man," while many later manuscripts read "the Son of God."
notes.9:36: The Greek vocative kyrie can mean either "sir" (as a respectful address prior to recognition) or "Lord" (as in v. 38, where the man worships Him).
notes.10:8: The phrase "before Me" is omitted in several early manuscripts, though strongly attested in P66, Vaticanus, and Alexandrinus; in context it points to self-appointed false shepherds rather than the Old Testament prophets.
notes.10:22: "The Feast of Dedication" (Greek ta enkainia) refers to Hanukkah, the winter festival commemorating the rededication of the Jerusalem temple in 164 BC under Judas Maccabeus.
notes.10:24: "Keep us in suspense" translates the Greek idiom literally meaning "lift up our soul."
notes.10:29: The critical Greek text uses neuter forms (ho ... meizon), literally "What My Father has given Me is greater than all," whereas another major textual tradition reads masculine forms ("My Father, who has given them to Me, is greater than all").
notes.10:30: The Greek word for "one" (hen) is neuter rather than masculine, indicating unity of essence and action while preserving the distinction of persons between Father and Son.
notes.11:12: Greek "sōthēsetai" literally means "will be saved" and is used here by the disciples in its medical sense ("will recover"), creating typical Johannine irony regarding spiritual salvation.
notes.11:18: Fifteen stadia is roughly two miles (about three kilometers).
notes.11:33: The Greek verb "enebrimēsato" conveys intense emotional agitation—often indignation or anger as well as deep distress—and "etaraxen heauton" literally reads "troubled Himself."
notes.11:35: In contrast to the loud weeping ("klaiō") of Mary and the mourners in verses 31 and 33, John uses "edakrysen" (its only New Testament occurrence), literally meaning "shed tears."
notes.11:48: Greek "topos" ("place") here refers specifically to the Jerusalem temple as the holy place.
notes.12:3: The rare Greek adjective pistikēs modifying nard is debated; it most likely means "genuine" or "pure" (unadulterated), though some take it to mean "liquid" or a commercial designation for a variety of nard.
notes.12:7: The Greek clause hina ... tērēsē ("so that she may keep it") is elliptical and debated; it may imply keeping what remains for Jesus' burial or function imperativally ("let her keep it for the day of My burial").
notes.12:27: "Father, save Me from this hour" can be understood either as a genuine plea immediately submitted to God's purpose or as a deliberative question continuing "what shall I say?" (i.e., "Shall I say, 'Father, save Me from this hour'?").
notes.12:43: Greek doxa ("glory") here carries the sense of honor, praise, or approval from people versus from God, while deliberately echoing the "glory" Isaiah saw in v. 41.
notes.13:1: Greek eis telos can mean either "to the end" (temporally, through His death) or "to the utmost," and both nuances may be intended here.
notes.13:2: Greek literally reads "having already put into the heart" without a possessive pronoun; it is usually understood as Judas's heart, though some take it as the devil's own purpose.
notes.13:10: Some early manuscripts omit "except to wash his feet" (ei me tous podas), reading simply "has no need to wash."
notes.13:19: Greek ego eimi literally reads "I am," echoing the divine self-declaration in the Greek Old Testament (e.g., Isa 43:10), though it can also be understood as "I am He."
notes.13:32: Some manuscripts include "If God has been glorified in Him" at the start of this verse, which is omitted in the earliest witnesses.
notes.14:1: Both occurrences of Greek pisteuete are ambiguous in form between indicative ("you believe") and imperative ("believe").
notes.14:2: Following the statement punctuation of the critical text, hoti is translated causally ("because I am going..."); alternatively, it may introduce a question ("would I have told you that I am going...?").
notes.14:14: Some manuscripts omit "Me" (me), reading "If you ask anything in My name."
notes.14:16: Greek parakletos designates one called alongside to assist, intercede, or plead a case, rendered "Advocate" (also commonly translated "Helper" or "Counselor").
notes.14:17: Greek uses neuter pronouns here to agree grammatically with neuter pneuma ("Spirit"), rendered with masculine personal pronouns reflecting the Spirit's personhood (cf. masculine ekeinos in 14:26).
notes.15:2: Greek airei is most commonly rendered "takes away," though some interpreters suggest "lifts up." The verb kathairei ("prunes" or "cleanses") creates a wordplay with katharoi ("clean") in verse 3.
notes.15:10: The Greek text reads "the Father's commandments" without the possessive pronoun "My."
notes.15:26: Greek parakletos ("Advocate") denotes one called alongside to assist, intercede, or counsel, and is also translated "Helper" or "Counselor."
notes.16:8: Greek elegxei ("will convict") carries a forensic range of meaning that includes exposing guilt, proving wrong, and convicting.
notes.16:13: The Greek text reads the future tense akousei ("will hear"), highlighting the Spirit's ongoing reception and declaration of what He receives.
notes.16:23: In this Greek text, "in My name" follows "He will give to you," connecting the phrase directly to the Father's giving rather than only to the disciples' asking.
notes.16:27: The Greek text reads "from God" rather than "from the Father," matching the disciples' confession in verse 30.
notes.17:2: The Greek uses a neuter singular collective ("all that You have given Him," similarly in 17:24) resumed by a plural pronoun ("them"), presenting believers both as a unified gift and as individual recipients of eternal life.
notes.17:11: The critical Greek text reads the singular relative pronoun referring back to "Your name" ("Your name that You have given Me," as also in 17:12), whereas some later manuscripts read a plural pronoun referring to the disciples.
notes.17:15: The Greek phrase "from the evil one" is grammatically ambiguous between masculine ("the evil one") and neuter ("evil"), though Johannine usage elsewhere favors the personal adversary.
notes.17:17: The Greek verb rendered "consecrate" (and "consecrated" in 17:19) means to set apart as holy for God's purpose, sharing the same root as "Holy Father" in 17:11.
notes.18:3: A "cohort" formally designated a Roman military unit of roughly six hundred soldiers, though the term could also refer to a smaller detachment led by a commander (18:12).
notes.18:5: Jesus' reply "I am" (repeated in 18:6, 8) functions both as ordinary self-identification ("I am he") and as a resonant echo of the divine self-declaration in John, directly contrasting with Peter's "I am not" in 18:17 and 18:25.
notes.18:24: The Greek verb is a simple past ("sent") rather than an explicit pluperfect, reflecting the narrative sequence in which Annas—who retained the courtesy title "high priest" after leaving office—interrogated Jesus before sending Him on to Caiaphas.
notes.18:37: The Greek wording "You say that I am a king" can also be construed as "You say so, because I am a king"; in either reading, Jesus affirms His kingship while reframing it around bearing witness to the truth rather than political revolt.
notes.19:13: The verb ἐκάθισεν can be read intransitively ("sat down on the judgment seat") or transitively ("seated Him on the judgment seat"); "in Hebrew" (Ἑβραϊστί) refers here to the Aramaic or Hebrew spoken in Judea.
notes.19:14: "The sixth hour" is about noon by Jewish daylight reckoning from sunrise, or about 6:00 a.m. if Roman reckoning from midnight is used.
notes.19:25: Literally "Mary of Clopas," usually understood as the wife of Clopas; commentators also debate whether three or four women are listed depending on whether she is identified with Jesus' mother's sister.
notes.19:39: A Roman pound (λίτρα) weighed about 12 ounces (327 grams), so a hundred pounds equals roughly 75 modern pounds (34 kilograms).
notes.20:17: Greek Μή μου ἅπτου uses a present imperative with μή, often indicating the cessation of an action already underway ("Stop holding on to Me" or "Do not keep clinging to Me") rather than a blanket prohibition against touching.
notes.20:22: Greek πνεῦμα ἅγιον is anarthrous ("Holy Spirit"), and the verb ἐνεφύσησεν ("breathed on/into") echoes the Septuagint wording of Genesis 2:7, where God breathes life into humanity.
notes.20:23: The perfect passive verbs ἀφέωνται ("have been forgiven") and κεκράτηνται ("have been retained") denote an established, abiding state.
notes.20:31: The Greek text reads the present subjunctive πιστεύητε ("may believe" or "may continue believing") rather than the aorist variant πιστεύσητε ("may come to believe").
notes.21:5: Greek προσφάγιον denotes food eaten with bread, especially fish; the negative particle μή frames the question as expecting a negative answer.
notes.21:7: In ancient usage, Greek γυμνός ("naked") often referred to someone stripped of his outer garment and wearing only an undergarment or loincloth while working.
notes.21:15: Greek πλέον τούτων ("more than these") is syntactically ambiguous and may refer to the other disciples, to the fishing boats and catch, or to the other disciples' love for Jesus.
notes.21:17: Across verses 15-17, the Greek alternates between ἀγαπάω and φιλέω ("love"), βόσκω ("feed") and ποιμαίνω ("shepherd"), ἀρνία ("lambs"), πρόβατα ("sheep"), and προβάτια ("little sheep"), as well as οἶδα and γινώσκω ("know"), illustrating John's characteristic stylistic variation.
